title.zh: 卷一百二十四 志第七十七 禮二十七
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 志第七十七 禮二十七 Volume 124 Treatises 77: Rites 27

sentences.zh: 禮二十七

translations.literal: Rites 27
translations.idiomatic: Rites 27

sentences.zh: （凶禮三）〉

translations.literal: (Mourning Rites III)
translations.idiomatic: (Mourning Rites III)

sentences.zh: ○外國喪禮及入吊儀諸臣喪葬等儀

translations.literal: ○ Rites for foreign mourning, protocols for entering to offer condolences, officials' funerals, and similar ceremonies
translations.idiomatic: ○ Rites for Mourning in Foreign States, Condolence Reception Protocol, Officials' Funerals, and Related Ceremonies

sentences.zh: 凡外國喪，告哀使至，有司擇日設次於內東門之北隅，命官攝太常卿及博士讚禮。

translations.literal: Whenever a foreign state had a bereavement and a mourning-announcement envoy arrived, the relevant offices chose a day and set up a tent at the northeast corner inside the Inner Eastern Gate, appointing officials to act as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Masters of Ceremony to direct the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a foreign power suffered a death and sent an envoy to announce mourning, the responsible offices chose a day and pitched a tent at the northeast corner inside the Inner Eastern Gate, with officials deputizing as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ritual masters to conduct the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 俟太常 卿奏請，即向其國而哭之，五舉音而止。

translations.literal: After the acting Director of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized and requested permission, [the emperor] then faced that country and wailed; he stopped after five utterances of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Once the acting Director of Imperial Sacrifices had memorialized and received approval, the emperor turned toward that state and wailed, stopping after five cries of mourning.

sentences.zh: 皇帝未釋素服，人使朝見，不宣班，不舞蹈，不謝麵天顏，引當殿，喝「拜」，兩拜，奏聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: While the emperor had not yet doffed plain mourning dress, when envoys from that state had an audience, the court roster was not announced, they did not perform the dance obeisance, they did not give thanks for viewing the imperial countenance; they were led before the hall, called to "Bow," performed two bows, and memorialized for the Sacred Person's ten thousand blessings.
translations.idiomatic: So long as the emperor had not yet laid aside plain mourning dress, envoys from the bereaved state who came to audience were not announced in the full court roster, did not perform the dance obeisance, and did not give thanks for beholding the imperial face; they were led before the hall, called to bow twice, and offered a memorial wishing the Sacred Person ten thousand blessings.

sentences.zh: 又喝「拜」，兩拜，隨 拜萬歲。

translations.literal: Again called to "Bow," they bowed twice and then bowed for ten thousand years [of reign].
translations.idiomatic: They were again called to bow twice, then bowed in homage for the emperor's longevity.

sentences.zh: 或增賜茶藥及傳宣撫問，即出班致詞，訖，歸位。

translations.literal: If additionally bestowed tea and medicine or an imperial message of consolation, they stepped out of formation to deliver an address; when finished they returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: If tea and medicine or an imperial message of consolation were additionally granted, they stepped out of formation to deliver an address and, when finished, returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 又喝「拜」，兩拜，隨拜萬歲。

translations.literal: Again called to "Bow," they bowed twice and then bowed for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: They were again called to bow twice and then bowed in homage for the emperor's longevity.

sentences.zh: 喝「祗候」，退。

translations.literal: Called to "Pay respects," and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Called to pay their respects, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年十二月，北朝皇太后凶訃， 遣使來告哀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, news arrived of the death of the Northern Court's empress dowager; an envoy was dispatched to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1009), word came that the Liao empress dowager had died, and the Khitan court sent envoys to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔遣官迓之，廢朝七日，擇日備禮舉哀成服，禮官詳定儀注以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials to meet them; court audiences were suspended for seven days; a day was chosen to prepare the ritual of wailing and putting on mourning dress; the ritual officers worked out the protocol in detail and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials to receive the envoys, suspended court audiences for seven days, and set a day for the full ritual of wailing and donning mourning dress; the ritual officers drafted the protocol in detail and reported it.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝常服乘輿詣幕殿，俟時釋常服，服素服，白羅衫、黑銀帶、素紗軟腳襆 頭。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor rode in ordinary dress to the tent hall; when the time came he removed ordinary dress and wore plain mourning dress: white silk robe, black silver belt, and plain gauze soft-foot headwrap.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor rode to the tent hall in ordinary dress; at the appointed hour he removed it and put on plain mourning: a white silk robe, black silver belt, and plain gauze soft-foot headwrap.

sentences.zh: 太常卿跪，奏請皇帝為北朝皇太后凶訃至掛服，又奏請五舉音。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices knelt and memorialized requesting the emperor to don mourning dress for the arrival of news of the Northern Court empress dowager's death, and again memorialized requesting five utterances of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices knelt and asked the emperor to put on mourning for the Liao empress dowager's death, then requested five cries of mourning.

sentences.zh: 文武百僚進名奉慰，退幕殿。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of all ranks advanced their names to offer condolences; they withdrew to the tent hall.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of every rank presented their names to offer condolences, then withdrew to the tent hall.

sentences.zh: 仍遣使祭奠吊慰。

translations.literal: Envoys were still dispatched to offer sacrificial rites and condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The court also dispatched envoys to perform sacrificial rites and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，契丹賀正使為本國皇太 後成服，所司設幕次、香、酒及衰服、絰、杖等，禮直官引使、副已下詣位，北向再拜。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the Khitan envoy congratulating the New Year was in full mourning for his state's empress dowager; the relevant offices set up a tent, incense, wine, and mourning garments including hemp bands and staff; ritual officers led the envoy, vice-envoy, and those below to their positions facing north and bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, the Khitan New Year's envoy was observing full mourning for his state's empress dowager; the responsible offices set up a tent with incense, wine, mourning garments, hemp bands, and staffs, and ritual officers led the envoy, his deputy, and their party to their places, where they faced north and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 班首詣前，執盞跪奠，俯伏，興，歸位，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The formation leader went forward, took the cup kneeling to offer libation, prostrated himself, rose, returned to position; all bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation stepped forward, took the cup, knelt to offer libation, prostrated himself, rose, and returned to his place; all bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 俟使已下俱衰服、絰、 杖，成服訖，禮直官再引各依位北向，舉哭盡哀。

translations.literal: After the envoy and those below had all put on mourning garments, hemp bands, and staff and completed putting on mourning dress, ritual officers again led each to his position facing north and wailed to exhaustion of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoy and his party had all donned mourning garments, hemp bands, and staffs and completed the full mourning dress, ritual officers again led each man to his place facing north, where they wailed until grief was spent.

sentences.zh: 班首少前，去杖，跪，奠酒訖，執杖，俯伏，興，歸位。

translations.literal: The formation leader stepped slightly forward, set aside the staff, knelt, offered wine; when finished took up the staff, prostrated himself, rose, returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The formation leader stepped slightly forward, set aside his staff, knelt and offered wine; when finished he took up the staff again, prostrated himself, rose, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 焚紙馬，皆舉哭，再拜畢，各還次，服吉服，歸驛。

translations.literal: Paper horses were burned; all wailed; when the second bows were finished each returned to his tent, changed into auspicious dress, and went back to the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: Paper horses were burned; all wailed; when the second bows were completed each returned to his tent, changed into ordinary dress, and went back to the relay station.

sentences.zh: 天聖九年六月，契丹使來告哀。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Tiansheng, a Khitan envoy came to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Tiansheng (1031), a Khitan envoy arrived to announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 禮官詳定：北朝凶訃，宜於西上閣門引來使奉書，令閣門使一員跪受承進，宰臣、樞密使已下待制已上，並就都亭驛吊慰。

translations.literal: The ritual officers worked out in detail: for news of death in the Northern Court, the incoming envoy presenting the document should be led in at the Western Upper Pavilion Gate; one Gate Department attendant was to kneel to receive and present it; the chief ministers, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and all from Attendant-in-Waiting upward were all to go to the Capital Pavilion Station to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers determined the protocol: for a death in the Liao court, the mourning envoy should be led in at the Western Upper Pavilion Gate to present his document, with one Gate Department attendant kneeling to receive and forward it; the chief ministers, the Commissioner of Military Affairs, and all officials from Attendant-in-Waiting rank upward were to offer condolences at the Capital Pavilion Station.

sentences.zh: 七月一 日，使者耶律乞石至，帝與皇太后發哀苑中，使者自驛赴左掖門入，至左升龍門下馬，入北偏門階下，行至右升龍北偏門，入朝堂西偏門，至文德殿門上奉書。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month the envoy Yelü Qishi arrived; the emperor and empress dowager began mourning in the palace garden; the envoy went from the relay station to enter through the Left Flank Gate, dismounted at the Left Ascending Dragon Gate, entered below the north side gate steps, proceeded to the north side gate of the Right Ascending Dragon, entered the west side gate of the Audience Hall, and at the gate of the Hall of Literary Virtue presented the document.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month the envoy Yelü Qishi arrived; the emperor and empress dowager began mourning in the palace garden; the envoy left the relay station, entered through the Left Flank Gate, dismounted at the Left Ascending Dragon Gate, passed through the north side gates and the west side gate of the Audience Hall, and presented his document at the gate of the Hall of Literary Virtue.

sentences.zh: 太常 博士二員與禮直官讚引入文德殿西偏門階下，行至西上閣門外階下，面北跪，進書。

translations.literal: Two Masters of Ceremony from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ritual officers directing the ceremony led him in below the west side gate steps of the Hall of Literary Virtue, proceeded to below the steps outside the Western Upper Pavilion Gate, knelt facing north, and presented the document.
translations.idiomatic: Two Masters of Ceremony and ritual officers led him in below the west side gate of the Hall of Literary Virtue, then to the steps outside the Western Upper Pavilion Gate, where they knelt facing north and presented the document.

sentences.zh: 閣門使跪受承進。

translations.literal: The Gate Department attendant knelt to receive and present it.
translations.idiomatic: A Gate Department attendant knelt to receive and forward it.

sentences.zh: 太常博士、禮直官退。

translations.literal: The Masters of Ceremony and ritual officers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Ceremony and ritual officers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 使者入西上閣門殿後偏門，入宣祐西偏 門，行赴內東門柱廊中間，過幕次祗候，朝見訖，赴崇政殿門幕次祗候，朝見皇太后訖，出。

translations.literal: The envoy entered through the rear side gate of the Western Upper Pavilion Gate hall, entered the west side gate of Xuanyou, proceeded to the middle of the pillar corridor at the Inner Eastern Gate, passed the tent to pay respects and wait; after the audience was finished he went to the tent at the Gate of the Hall of Esteeming Governance to pay respects and wait; after the audience with the empress dowager was finished he departed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered through the rear side gate of the Western Upper Pavilion Gate hall and the west side gate of Xuanyou, proceeded to the pillar corridor at the Inner Eastern Gate, waited at the mourning tent, completed his audience with the emperor, then waited at the tent by the Gate of the Hall of Esteeming Governance for his audience with the empress dowager, and departed.

sentences.zh: 三日，近臣慰乞石於驛。

translations.literal: On the third day, close ministers offered condolences to Qishi at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day, close ministers offered condolences to Qishi at the relay station.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年正月，契丹告國母哀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiayou, the Khitan announced mourning for the state mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jiayou (1058), the Khitan court announced the death of the state mother.

sentences.zh: 使人到闕入見，皇帝問云：「卿離北朝日，侄皇帝悲苦之中，聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached the capital and had an audience, the emperor inquired: "On the day you left the Northern Court, while the nephew emperor was amid grief, was the Sacred Person in ten thousand blessings?"
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached the capital and was received in audience, the emperor asked: "On the day you left the Liao court, while the nephew emperor was in the depths of grief, was his Sacred Person in good health?"

sentences.zh: 」朝辭日，即云：「皇帝傳語北朝侄皇帝，嬸太皇太后上仙，遠勞人使訃告。

translations.literal: " On the day of farewell audience he said: "The emperor conveys a message to the Northern Court's nephew emperor: the aunt grand empress dowager has ascended as an immortal; you have taken the trouble to send envoys from afar to announce the death."
translations.idiomatic: " On the day of his farewell audience the emperor said: "Convey to the Liao nephew emperor: your aunt the grand empress dowager has passed away; we are grateful that you sent envoys from afar to announce the mourning."

sentences.zh: 春寒，善保聖 躬。

translations.literal: The spring is cold; take good care of the Sacred Person."
translations.idiomatic: The spring is still cold; take good care of yourself."

sentences.zh: 」中書、樞密以下、待制已上赴驛吊慰，云：「竊審北朝太皇太后上仙，伏惟悲苦。

translations.literal: " The Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, and all from Attendant-in-Waiting upward went to the relay station to offer condolences, saying: "We have learned that the Northern Court's grand empress dowager has ascended as an immortal; we can only imagine your grief."
translations.idiomatic: " Officials of the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission from Attendant-in-Waiting rank upward went to the relay station to offer condolences, saying: "We have learned that the Liao grand empress dowager has passed away; we can only imagine your grief."

sentences.zh: 」五月，獻遺留物。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month they presented bequeathed goods.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month they presented goods left by the deceased.

sentences.zh: 明道元年十一月二十四日敕：夏王趙德明 薨，特輟朝三日，令司天監定舉哀掛服日辰。

translations.literal: Edict of the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Mingdao: King of Xia Zhao Deming has died; court audiences are specially suspended for three days; the Directorate of Astronomy is ordered to fix the day and hour for wailing and donning mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Mingdao (1032): Zhao Deming, King of Xia, has died; court audiences are specially suspended for three days, and the Directorate of Astronomy is to set the day and hour for wailing and donning mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 其日，乘輿至幕殿，服素服。

translations.literal: On that day the imperial carriage went to the tent hall; [the emperor] wore plain mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor rode to the tent hall in plain mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 太常博士引太常卿當御坐前跪，奏請皇帝為夏王趙德明薨舉哀，又奏請十五舉音，又奏請 可止。

translations.literal: A Master of Ceremony led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to kneel before the imperial seat and memorialized requesting the emperor to wail for the death of King of Xia Zhao Deming, again memorialized requesting fifteen utterances of grief, and again memorialized requesting that he might stop.
translations.idiomatic: A Master of Ceremony led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to kneel before the throne and asked the emperor to wail for Zhao Deming's death, then requested fifteen cries of mourning, and finally asked that he might stop.

sentences.zh: 文武百僚進名奉慰。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of all ranks advanced their names to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of every rank presented their names to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 告哀使、副已下朝見，首領並從人作兩班見。

translations.literal: The mourning-announcement envoy, vice-envoy, and those below had an audience; the leaders and attendants were received in two formations.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning envoy, his deputy, and their party were received in audience; the leaders and attendants were arranged in two formations.

sentences.zh: 先首領見，兩拜後，班首奏聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: The leaders were received first; after two bows the formation leader memorialized for the Sacred Person's ten thousand blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The leaders were received first; after two bows the head of the formation wished the Sacred Person ten thousand blessings.

sentences.zh: 又兩拜，隨拜萬歲。

translations.literal: Again two bows, followed by bowing for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed twice again, then bowed in homage for the emperor's longevity.

sentences.zh: 喝賜例物酒食，跪受。

translations.literal: Called to receive the customary bestowal of goods, wine, and food; they knelt to receive.
translations.idiomatic: They were called forward to receive the customary gifts of goods, wine, and food and knelt to accept them.

sentences.zh: 起，又兩 拜，隨拜萬歲。

translations.literal: They rose, again bowed twice, and bowed for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, bowed twice again, and bowed in homage for the emperor's longevity.

sentences.zh: 喝「各祗候」，退。

translations.literal: Called "Each pay respects," and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Called to pay their respects, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 從人儀同。

translations.literal: The attendants followed the same protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants followed the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太后至幕殿，釋常服，白羅大袖、白羅大帶，舉哀如皇帝儀。

translations.literal: That day the empress dowager came to the tent hall, removed ordinary dress, wore white silk large sleeves and white silk large belt, and wailed according to the emperor's protocol.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the empress dowager came to the tent hall, removed her ordinary dress, put on white silk large sleeves and a white silk belt, and wailed according to the emperor's protocol.

sentences.zh: 其遣使致祭吊慰，如契丹。

translations.literal: The dispatch of envoys to perform sacrifice and offer condolences followed the Khitan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The dispatch of envoys to perform sacrifice and offer condolences followed the same protocol used for the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 所司預於滋福殿設大行皇帝神御坐，又於稍東設御坐。

translations.literal: The relevant offices beforehand set up the spirit seat of the late emperor in the Hall of Blessings and Fortune, and also set up an imperial seat slightly to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices beforehand set up the late emperor's spirit seat in the Hall of Blessings and Fortune, with an imperial seat placed slightly to the east.

sentences.zh: 祭奠吊慰使、副並素服，由西上閣門入，陳禮物於庭。

translations.literal: The sacrificial condolence envoys and vice-envoys all in plain mourning dress entered through the Western Upper Pavilion Gate and displayed ritual gifts in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial and condolence envoys and their deputies, all in plain mourning dress, entered through the Western Upper Pavilion Gate and displayed their ritual gifts in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 中書、門下、樞密院並立於殿下，再拜訖，升殿，分 東西立。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, Chancellery, and Military Affairs Commission all stood below the hall; when the second bows were finished they ascended the hall and stood divided east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, Chancellery, and Military Affairs Commission all stood below the hall; after bowing twice they ascended and took their places on the east and west sides.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、閣門舍人讚引耶律三隱等詣神御坐前階下，俟殿上簾卷，使、副等並舉哭，殿上皆哭。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and Gate Department attendants directing the ceremony led Yelü Sanyin and others to below the steps before the spirit seat; when the curtain above the hall was rolled up the envoys and vice-envoys all wailed, and all above the hall wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and Gate Department attendants led Yelü Sanyin and his party to the steps before the spirit seat; when the hall curtain was raised the envoys and their deputies all wailed, and everyone in the hall wailed with them.

sentences.zh: 再拜訖，引升殿西階，詣神御坐前上香、奠茶酒。

translations.literal: When the second bows were finished they were led up the west steps of the hall to before the spirit seat to offer incense and present tea and wine.
translations.idiomatic: After bowing twice they were led up the west steps to the spirit seat to offer incense and present tea and wine.

sentences.zh: 貽謀跪讀 祭文畢，降階，復位，又舉哭，再拜訖，稍東立。

translations.literal: Yimou knelt and read the sacrificial text to completion, descended the steps, returned to position, wailed again, and when the second bows were finished stood slightly to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Yimou knelt and read the sacrificial text to completion, descended the steps, returned to his place, wailed again, and after bowing twice stood slightly to the east.

sentences.zh: 俟皇太后升坐，中書、樞密院起居畢，簾外侍立。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager ascended her seat and the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission had finished their greetings, they stood in attendance outside the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager had taken her seat and the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission had paid their greetings, they stood in attendance outside the curtain.

sentences.zh: 舍人引吊慰祭奠使、副朝見。

translations.literal: Attendants led the condolence and sacrificial envoys and vice-envoys in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led the condolence and sacrificial envoys and their deputies in for audience.

sentences.zh: 殿上舉哭，左右皆哭。

translations.literal: Those above the hall wailed; those to left and right all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the hall wailed, and everyone on either side wailed with them.

sentences.zh: 吊慰使、副 蕭日新等升殿進書訖，降坐。

translations.literal: The condolence envoys and vice-envoys Xiao Rixin and others ascended the hall and presented their documents; when finished they descended from the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence envoys Xiao Rixin and his deputies ascended the hall and presented their documents, then descended.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝升坐，中書、樞密院起居畢，升殿侍立。

translations.literal: After the emperor ascended his seat and the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission had finished their greetings, they ascended the hall to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had taken his seat and the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission had paid their greetings, they ascended to stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 舍人引吊慰祭奠使、副朝見。

translations.literal: Attendants led the condolence and sacrificial envoys and vice-envoys in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led the condolence and sacrificial envoys and their deputies in for audience.

sentences.zh: 皇帝舉哭，左右皆哭。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed; those to left and right all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wailed, and everyone on either side wailed with him.

sentences.zh: 吊慰使、副耶律寧等升殿進書訖， 賜三隱等襲衣、冠帶、器幣、鞍馬，隨行舍利、牙校等衣服、銀帶、器幣有差。

translations.literal: The condolence envoys and vice-envoys Yelü Ning and others ascended the hall and presented their documents; Sanyin and others were bestowed court robes, cap and belt, vessels and silks, and saddled horses; accompanying śarīra [relic] guardians, military officers, and others received graded gifts of clothing, silver belts, vessels, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence envoys Yelü Ning and his deputies ascended the hall and presented their documents; Sanyin and his party were granted court robes, caps and belts, vessels, silks, and saddled horses, while accompanying relic guardians, military officers, and others received graded gifts of clothing, silver belts, vessels, and silks.

sentences.zh: 吊慰使、副蕭日新等復詣承明殿，俟皇太后升坐，中書、樞密院侍立如儀。

translations.literal: The condolence envoys and vice-envoys Xiao Rixin and others again went to the Hall of Illuminated Succession; after the empress dowager ascended her seat the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission stood in attendance according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence envoys Xiao Rixin and his deputies then went to the Hall of Illuminated Succession; once the empress dowager had taken her seat the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission stood in attendance as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 舍人引蕭 日新等升殿進問聖候書畢，賜銀器、衣著有差。

translations.literal: Attendants led Xiao Rixin and others to ascend the hall and present the document inquiring after the Sacred Person; when finished they were bestowed silver vessels and clothing in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led Xiao Rixin and his party up to present their document inquiring after the empress dowager's health; they were then granted silver vessels and clothing in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 仍就客省賜三隱等茶酒，又令樞密副使張士遜別會三隱等伴宴於都亭驛。

translations.literal: They were still at the Reception Office bestowed tea and wine on Sanyin and others; moreover the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Zhang Shixun was ordered separately to host Sanyin and others in a companion banquet at the Capital Pavilion Station.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyin and his party were additionally granted tea and wine at the Reception Office, and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Zhang Shixun was ordered to host a separate banquet for them at the Capital Pavilion Station.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，契丹使來賀乾元節，命先進書奠梓宮，見於東階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Khitan envoys came to congratulate the Qianyuan Festival; they were ordered first to present documents and offer libation at the coffin palace, and were received on the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Khitan envoys arrived to congratulate the Qianyuan Festival; they were ordered first to present documents and offer libation at the imperial coffin, and were received on the east steps.

sentences.zh: 放夏國使人見，客省以書幣入，後吊慰使見殿門外。

translations.literal: The Xia envoys were allowed an audience; the Reception Office brought in documents and silks; afterward the condolence envoys were received outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia envoys were granted an audience; the Reception Office brought in their documents and gifts; afterward the condolence envoys were received outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 契丹祭奠使見於皇儀殿東廂，群臣慰於門外。

translations.literal: The Khitan sacrificial envoys were received in the east wing of the Hall of Imperial Rites; the assembled ministers offered condolences outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sacrificial envoys were received in the east wing of the Hall of Imperial Rites, while the assembled ministers offered condolences outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 使人辭於紫宸殿，命坐賜茶。

translations.literal: The envoys took leave at the Hall of Purple Brightness; they were ordered to be seated and bestowed tea.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys took their leave at the Hall of Purple Brightness, were seated, and granted tea.

sentences.zh: 故事賜酒五行，自是，終諒闇，皆賜茶。

translations.literal: By precedent wine of five rounds was bestowed; from this time through the entire mourning period, only tea was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent five rounds of wine were served; from this time onward, throughout the entire mourning period, only tea was granted.

sentences.zh: 神宗之喪，夏國陳慰使丁努嵬名謨鐸、副使呂則、陳聿精等進慰表於皇儀門外，退赴紫宸殿門，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: At the mourning for Emperor Shenzong, the Xia envoys presenting condolences Ding Nuweiming Moduo, vice-envoy Lü Ze, Chen Yujing, and others presented their condolence memorial outside the Gate of Imperial Rites, withdrew to the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness, and were bestowed silks in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Shenzong's mourning, the Xia condolence envoys Ding Nuweiming Moduo, his deputy Lü Ze, Chen Yujing, and others presented their condolence memorial outside the Gate of Imperial Rites, then withdrew to the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness, where they received graded gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，高麗入貢，有太皇太后表及進奉物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Koryŏ came to offer tribute, including a memorial to the grand empress dowager and tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era, Koryŏ sent tribute including a memorial to the grand empress dowager and presentation goods.

sentences.zh: 樞密院請遵故事，惟答以皇帝回諭敕書。

translations.literal: The Military Affairs Commission requested following precedent: reply only with the emperor's responsive edict letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Affairs Commission requested that precedent be followed: reply only with the emperor's responsive edict.

sentences.zh: 已而宣仁聖烈太后崩，禮部、太常、閣門同詳定：高麗奉慰使人於小祥前後到闕，令於紫宸殿門見，客省受表以進，賜器物、酒饌，退，並常服、黑帶、不佩魚。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Sagely and Fierce Grand Empress Dowager Xuanren died; the Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Gate Department jointly worked out in detail: if Koryŏ condolence envoys reached the capital around the time of the lesser auspicious rite, they were to be received at the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness; the Reception Office was to receive the memorial and present it; they were to be bestowed vessels, wine, and food and withdraw—all in ordinary dress, black belt, without wearing the fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Sagely and Fierce Grand Empress Dowager Xuanren died; the Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Gate Department jointly determined the protocol: if Koryŏ condolence envoys arrived around the time of the lesser auspicious rite, they were to be received at the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness; the Reception Office would receive their memorial and present it; they would be granted vessels, wine, and food and withdraw—all in ordinary dress with black belts, without wearing the fish tally.

sentences.zh: 候見罷，純吉服。

translations.literal: After waiting until the audience was finished, [they changed into] pure auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: After the audience was completed, they changed into full ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年，金國吊祭使到闕，惟皇帝先詣梓宮行燒香禮，及使入門祭訖，皆就幄舉哭外，陳設行事並如先朝舊儀。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi, Jin condolence and sacrificial envoys reached the capital; only the emperor first went to the coffin palace to perform the incense-burning rite, and after the envoys entered the gate and finished sacrifice, apart from all wailing at the mourning tent, the display of objects and conduct of the ceremony all followed the former court's old protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi (1187), Jin condolence and sacrificial envoys reached the capital; apart from the emperor's prior visit to the coffin palace to burn incense and the wailing at the mourning tent after the envoys entered and completed their sacrifice, the display of ritual objects and conduct of the ceremony followed the protocols of earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 其奉辭日，有司亦先設神御坐及設香案、茶 酒、果食盤台於幾筵殿上。

translations.literal: On the day of their farewell audience, the relevant offices also beforehand set up the spirit seat and set out incense table, tea, wine, and fruit-food trays on the hall of the spirit couch.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of their farewell audience, the responsible offices also set up the spirit seat in advance, along with an incense table and trays of tea, wine, and fruit on the hall of the spirit couch.

sentences.zh: 宰執升殿分東西立，侍從官於殿下西面立。

translations.literal: The chief ministers ascended the hall and stood divided east and west; attendant officials stood on the west side below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers ascended the hall and took their places on the east and west sides; attendant officials stood on the west side below the hall.

sentences.zh: 使、副入門，殿上下皆哭，使、副升殿，哭止。

translations.literal: The envoys and vice-envoys entered the gate; all above and below the hall wailed; the envoys and vice-envoys ascended the hall and the wailing stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys and their deputies entered; everyone in the hall wailed; the envoys ascended the hall and the wailing ceased.

sentences.zh: 使、副詣神坐前一拜，上香、奠茶、三奠酒 畢，拜，興，讀祭文官跪讀祭文，一拜，興，殿上下皆哭。

translations.literal: The envoys and vice-envoys went before the spirit seat and bowed once, offered incense, presented tea, and completed three libations of wine; they bowed and rose; the official reading the sacrificial text knelt and read it, bowed once and rose; all above and below the hall wailed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys and their deputies approached the spirit seat and bowed once, offered incense, presented tea, and completed three libations of wine; they bowed and rose; the official reading the sacrificial text knelt, read it, bowed once and rose; everyone in the hall wailed.

sentences.zh: 使、副俱降，歸位立，又再拜訖，退。

translations.literal: The envoys and vice-envoys both descended, returned to position and stood, again bowed twice, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys and their deputies both descended, returned to their places, bowed twice again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸臣之喪，國製：諸王、公主、宗室將軍以上有疾，皆乘輿臨問。

translations.literal: For the mourning of various officials, state regulation: whenever princes, princesses, and imperial clansmen of General rank and above fell ill, the imperial carriage always went in person to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: For the mourning of officials, state regulation held that whenever princes, princesses, and imperial clansmen of General rank and above fell ill, the emperor always went in person to inquire after them.

sentences.zh: 如小疾在家，或幸其第，有至三四者。

translations.literal: For minor illness at home, [the emperor] might visit their residence; there were cases reaching three or four visits.
translations.idiomatic: For minor illnesses at home, the emperor might visit their residence, sometimes as many as three or four times.

sentences.zh: 其宮邸在禁中，多不時而往。

translations.literal: If their palace residence was within the Forbidden City, [he] often went at irregular hours.
translations.idiomatic: If their residence was within the Forbidden City, he often visited at irregular hours.

sentences.zh: 惟宰相、使相、駙馬都尉疾亟，幸其第，或賜勞加禮焉。

translations.literal: Only when the chief minister, commissioner with ministerial rank, or Commandant-in-Chief of the Imperial Sons-in-Law was gravely ill did [the emperor] visit their residence, sometimes bestowing consolation with added ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the chief minister, a commissioner holding ministerial rank, or the Commandant-in-Chief of the Imperial Sons-in-Law was gravely ill did the emperor visit their residence, sometimes bestowing additional gifts and ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年七月，宰相範質有疾，太祖親幸其第，賜黃金、銀、絹有差。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianlong, Chief Minister Fan Zhi fell ill; Taizu personally visited his residence and bestowed gold, silver, and silk in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianlong (960), Chief Minister Fan Zhi fell ill; Taizu personally visited his home and granted him graded gifts of gold, silver, and silk.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，趙普有疾，帝再往視，賜銀器、絹甚厚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Zhao Pu fell ill; the emperor went again to visit and bestowed silver vessels and silk in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao (969), Zhao Pu fell ill; the emperor visited him a second time and granted him a generous gift of silver vessels and silk.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，鎮寧軍節度楊信久病喑， 忽能言，帝異之，遽幸其第，加賜賚。

translations.literal: During the Taiping Xingguo era, Zhenning Army Commissioner Yang Xin had long been ill and mute; he suddenly could speak; the emperor marveled at this and hastened to visit his residence, adding to his bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era (976–983), Zhenning Army Commissioner Yang Xin had long been ill and unable to speak; when he suddenly regained his voice the emperor was astonished and hastened to his home with additional gifts.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年三月，鎮安軍節度使、駙馬都尉石保吉疾亟，帝將臨視之，其日大忌，宰相言於禮非便，遂遣內侍以諭保吉，明 日始臨省焉。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Zhen'an Army Commissioner and Commandant-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law Shi Baoji was gravely ill; the emperor was about to visit him in person, but that day was a major taboo day; the chief minister said it was not proper by ritual, so a palace attendant was sent to inform Baoji that the visit would begin only the next day.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1010), Zhen'an Army Commissioner and Commandant-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law Shi Baoji was gravely ill; the emperor intended to visit him, but that day was a major taboo day and the chief minister said a visit would be ritually improper, so a palace attendant was sent to inform Baoji that the emperor would visit the following day.

sentences.zh: 六月，幸翰林侍講學士邢昺第視疾，賜白金千兩、衣著千匹、名藥一奩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month [the emperor] visited the residence of Hanlin Academician-Reader Xing Bing to inquire after his illness, bestowing one thousand taels of white gold, one thousand bolts of clothing, and one casket of famous medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor visited Hanlin Academician-Reader Xing Bing at his home to inquire after his illness, granting him one thousand taels of white gold, one thousand bolts of clothing, and a casket of renowned medicines.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年十二月，詔頒新式，凡臨幸問疾者賜銀、絹，宰臣及樞 密使帶使相者二千五百兩匹，樞密使、使相二千兩匹，知樞密院事、參知政事、樞密副使、同知樞密院事一千五百兩匹，簽書樞密院事、同簽書樞密院事、宣徽使七 百五十兩匹，殿前都指揮使一千五百兩匹，駙馬都尉任使相以下者二千五百兩匹，任節度觀察留後以下者一千五百兩匹，並入內內侍省取賜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Xining, an edict promulgated new regulations: for all personal visits to inquire after illness, silver and silk were bestowed—chief ministers and Commissioners of Military Affairs holding ministerial rank received 2,500 taels and bolts; Commissioners of Military Affairs and commissioners with ministerial rank 2,000; Directors of the Military Affairs Commission, Vice Directors of the Secretariat, Vice Commissioners of Military Affairs, and Associate Directors 1,500; Signers of the Military Affairs Commission, Associate Signers, and Commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service 750; Commanders-in-Chief of the Palace Front Command 1,500; Commandants-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law holding ranks below commissioner with ministerial rank 2,500; those holding military commissioner ranks below Military Governor and Observation Commissioner 1,500—all to be taken and bestowed from the Inner Palace Attendant Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Xining (1074), an edict promulgated new regulations for gifts of silver and silk on personal visits to inquire after illness: chief ministers and Commissioners of Military Affairs holding ministerial rank received 2,500 taels and bolts; Commissioners of Military Affairs and commissioners with ministerial rank 2,000; Directors of the Military Affairs Commission, Vice Directors of the Secretariat, Vice Commissioners of Military Affairs, and Associate Directors 1,500; Signers of the Military Affairs Commission, Associate Signers, and Commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service 750; Commanders-in-Chief of the Palace Front Command 1,500; Commandants-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law below commissioner with ministerial rank 2,500; those below Military Governor and Observation Commissioner 1,500—all distributed through the Inner Palace Attendant Service.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨 奠。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage attends in person to pour libation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attends funerals in person to pour libation.

sentences.zh: 《太常新禮》：宰相、樞密、宣徽使、參知政事、樞密副使、駙馬都尉薨，皆臨幸奠酹，及發引，乘輿或再往。

translations.literal: New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: when the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, or Commandant-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law died, [the emperor] always visited in person to pour libation; at the departure of the coffin the imperial carriage sometimes went again.
translations.idiomatic: According to the New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, when the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, or Commandant-in-Chief of Imperial Sons-in-Law died, the emperor always visited in person to pour libation, and sometimes went again when the coffin was borne away.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，工部侍郎、樞密副使楊礪卒，即日冒 雨臨其喪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, Vice Minister of Works and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Li died; that same day [the emperor] braved the rain to attend his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999), Vice Minister of Works and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Li died; the emperor braved the rain that same day to attend his funeral.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，殿前都虞候、端州防禦使李繼和卒，真宗將臨其喪，以問宰臣，對曰：「繼和以品秩實無此禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Chief Commandant of the Palace Front Command and Duanzhou Defense Commissioner Li Jihe died; Emperor Zhenzong was about to attend his mourning and asked the chief minister, who replied: "By rank and grade Jihe in fact has no claim to this ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008), Chief Commandant of the Palace Front Command and Duanzhou Defense Commissioner Li Jihe died; Emperor Zhenzong intended to attend his funeral and asked the chief minister, who replied: "By rank and grade Jihe is not entitled to this honor."

sentences.zh: 陛下敦序外族，先朝亦嘗臨杜審瓊之喪， 於禮無嫌。

translations.literal: Your Majesty values ordering relations with affinal kin; the former court also once attended the mourning of Du Shenqiong—there is no objection in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty values ties with affinal kin, and the former court also attended the funeral of Du Shenqiong—there is no ritual objection."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，即日幸其第。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved and that day visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and visited his home that same day.

sentences.zh: 康定二年，右正言、知制誥吳育奏：「臣竊見車駕每有臨奠臣僚、宗戚之家，皆即時出幸，道路不戒，羽衛不全， 從官奔馳，眾目驚異。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangding, Right Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts Wu Yu memorialized: "Your servant has observed that whenever the imperial carriage attends the mourning of officials or imperial kin, it always sets out immediately; the roads are not secured, the guard of arms and feathers is incomplete, attendant officials rush about, and all eyes are startled."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangding (1041), Right Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts Wu Yu memorialized: "I have observed that whenever the imperial carriage attends the funeral of an official or imperial kinsman, it sets out immediately without securing the roads, without a full guard escort, with attendant officials rushing about—a sight that startles all who see it."

sentences.zh: 萬乘法駕，豈慎重之意乎？

translations.literal: The chariot of the lord of ten thousand—can this be an expression of careful regard?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the chariot of the Son of Heaven ought to express careful regard?"

sentences.zh: 雖震悼方切於皇慈；

translations.literal: Although shock and grief are still keen in the emperor's compassionate heart;
translations.idiomatic: Though the shock of bereavement weighs deeply upon Your Majesty's compassionate heart;

sentences.zh: 而舉動貴合乎經禮。

translations.literal: Yet movements and conduct ought to conform to the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: yet Your Majesty's actions ought above all to conform to canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣竊詳《通禮》舊儀，蓋俟喪家成服，然後臨奠，於事不迫，在禮亦宜。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately examined the old protocol in the Comprehensive Rites: it is generally a matter of waiting until the bereaved household has completed donning mourning garments, and then attending to offer libations; in practice there is no urgency, and in ritual this too is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the old protocol in the Comprehensive Rites, which generally calls for waiting until the bereaved family has completed dressing in mourning before the emperor attends to offer libations; this avoids undue haste and is ritually appropriate.

sentences.zh: 臣愚欲乞今後車駕如有臨奠去處，乞俟本家既斂成服，然後出幸，則恩意容典，詳而得中，警蹕羽儀，備之有素。

translations.literal: Your servant, in my ignorance, wish to request that hereafter, wherever the imperial carriage goes to attend libations, it be requested to wait until that household has both encoffined and completed mourning dress, and then set out on the imperial visit; then favor and ceremonial dignity will be measured and attain the mean, and the guard of the road and feathered insignia will be prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that hereafter, whenever the imperial carriage is to attend a funeral offering, it wait until the family has completed encoffinement and donned mourning dress before departing; thus imperial favor and ceremonial dignity will be both ample and properly measured, and the route guards and full guard escort will be prepared in advance.

sentences.zh: 」事下禮官議：「遭喪之家，有出殯日乃成服者， 恐至時難行臨奠。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the ritual officials for deliberation: "In bereaved households, there are cases in which mourning dress is only completed on the day of the departure for burial; we fear that at that time it will be difficult to conduct the libation visit.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the Board of Rites. They reported: "Some bereaved families do not complete mourning dress until the day of the funeral procession; we fear that at that point an imperial libation visit would be impracticable.

sentences.zh: 請自今聖駕臨奠臣僚、宗戚之家，若奏訃在交未前，即傳宣閣門，隻於當日令所屬候儀衛備，奏請車駕出幸；

translations.literal: We request that from now on, when the Sacred Person attends libations at the homes of officials or imperial kin, if the report of death arrives before the jiaowei hour, then an order be transmitted through the Gate of the Inner Portico, and on that day alone the responsible officials be directed to await readiness of guard and insignia, and memorialize requesting the imperial carriage to set out;
translations.idiomatic: We propose that hereafter, when the emperor attends a funeral at the home of an official or imperial kinsman, if word of death arrives before the jiaowei hour—that is, before late afternoon—the Palace Gate office should be notified at once so that the responsible officials can prepare the guard escort that same day and memorialize for the emperor's departure;

sentences.zh: 若奏訃在交未後，即次日臨奠。

translations.literal: If the report of death arrives after the jiaowei hour, then the libation visit shall take place the next day.
translations.idiomatic: If word arrives after the jiaowei hour, the imperial visit should take place the following day.

sentences.zh: 庶使 羽衛整肅，於事為宜。

translations.literal: Thus the feathered guards may be kept orderly and stern, and affairs will be suitably arranged.
translations.idiomatic: This will allow the guard escort to be properly assembled—a fitting arrangement for such occasions.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 其儀：乘輿自內出，千牛將軍四人執戈，一人執桃，一人執茢，前導。

translations.literal: The protocol: the imperial carriage sets out from within the palace; four Thousand-Ox Generals bear halberds, one bears a peach staff, and one bears a spiritual-herb staff, leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol was as follows: the imperial carriage departed from within the palace, preceded by four Thousand-Ox Generals bearing halberds, one with a peach-wood staff, and one with a spiritual-herb staff.

sentences.zh: 車駕將至所幸之第，讚禮者引喪主哭於大門內， 望見乘輿，止哭，再拜，立於庭。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to reach the residence visited, the ritual master led the chief mourner to wail inside the main gate; upon sighting the imperial carriage, wailing ceased, they bowed twice, and stood in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage approached the residence, the master of ceremonies led the chief mourner to wail inside the main gate. Upon sighting the carriage, the mourner ceased wailing, bowed twice, and stood in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至幕殿，改素服就臨，喪主內外再拜。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the curtained hall, he changed into plain white garments and approached to attend; the chief mourner and those inside and outside bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the curtained hall, the emperor changed into plain white mourning dress and approached to attend; the chief mourner and the household, within and without, bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝哭，十五舉音，喪主內外皆哭。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed, raising his voice fifteen times; the chief mourner and those inside and outside all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wailed, raising his voice fifteen times, and the chief mourner and entire household wailed with him.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣祭所三奠酒，喪主已下再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the offering site and poured libations three times; the chief mourner and those below bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeded to the offering site and poured libations three times; the chief mourner and all those in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝退，止 哭。

translations.literal: The emperor withdrew, and wailing ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew, wailing ceased.

sentences.zh: 從官進名奉慰。

translations.literal: Attendant officials advanced with their names to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials came forward to register their names and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 皇帝改常服還內。

translations.literal: The emperor changed back into ordinary dress and returned within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed back into ordinary dress and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 《通禮》著：皇帝臨諸王、妃、主、外祖父母、皇后父母、宗戚、貴臣等喪，出宮服常服，至所臨處變服素服。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Rites records: when the emperor attends the mourning of princes, consorts, princesses, maternal grandparents, the empress's parents, imperial kin, and honored ministers, he leaves the palace in ordinary dress and changes into plain white garments upon arriving at the place attended.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites stipulates that when attending the funerals of princes, consorts, princesses, maternal grandparents, the empress's parents, imperial kin, and high ministers, the emperor departs the palace in ordinary dress and changes into plain white mourning garments upon arrival.

sentences.zh: 《天聖喪葬令》：皇帝臨臣之喪，一品服錫衰，三品已上緦衰，四品已下疑衰。

translations.literal: The Tian Sheng Funeral Ordinances: when the emperor attends an official's mourning, he wears xī mourning for first rank, sī mourning for third rank and above, and yí mourning for fourth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian Sheng Funeral Ordinances specify that when attending an official's funeral, the emperor wears fine-cut mourning for deaths of first-rank officials, coarse hemp mourning for third rank and above, and standard hemp mourning for fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 皇太子臨吊三師、三少則錫衰，宮臣四品已上緦衰，五品已下疑衰。

translations.literal: When the crown prince attends to condole for the Three Preceptors and Three Junior Preceptors, he wears xī mourning; for palace officials of fourth rank and above, sī mourning; for fifth rank and below, yí mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince attends the funeral of a Three Preceptor or Three Junior Preceptor, he wears fine-cut mourning; for palace officials of fourth rank and above, coarse hemp mourning; for fifth rank and below, standard hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 輟朝之制。

translations.literal: Regulations for suspending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Suspension of Court Audiences.

sentences.zh: 《禮院例冊》：文武官一品、二品喪，輟視朝二日，於便殿舉哀掛服。

translations.literal: The Board of Rites precedent records: for the mourning of civil and military officials of first and second rank, court audiences are suspended for two days, and lamentation with donning of mourning garments is conducted in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Board of Rites precedent records, upon the death of a civil or military official of first or second rank, court audiences were suspended for two days, and the emperor performed lamentation and donned mourning dress in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 文武官三品喪，輟視朝一日，不舉哀掛服。

translations.literal: For civil and military officials of third rank, court audiences are suspended for one day, without lamentation or donning of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: For officials of third rank, court audiences were suspended for one day only, without lamentation or donning mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 然其車駕臨問並特輟朝日數，各係聖 恩。

translations.literal: Yet the number of days for suspension of court when the imperial carriage attends in inquiry, and special suspensions of court, each depend on imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: However, the number of days suspended when the emperor personally visited, or when extraordinary suspensions were granted, all depended on the emperor's special favor.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品喪皆以翰林學士已下為監護葬事，以內侍都知已下為同監護葬事。

translations.literal: For mourning of first and second rank, Hanlin Academicians and those below serve as supervisors of funeral affairs, and Palace eunuch commissioners-in-chief and those below serve as co-supervisors of funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For first- and second-rank deaths, a Hanlin Academician or lower served as supervisor of funeral arrangements, assisted by a eunuch commissioner-in-chief or lower as co-supervisor.

sentences.zh: 葬日，輟視朝一日，皆取旨後行。

translations.literal: On the burial day, court audiences are suspended for one day; all are implemented after receiving imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, court audiences were suspended for one day; all such measures were carried out only after receiving the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 慶曆五年四月，禮院奏：「準度支員外郎、集賢 校理知院曾公亮奏：『朝廷行輟朝禮，並乞以聞哀之明日輟朝，其假日便以充數，仍為永例。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Qingli, the Board of Rites memorialized: "In accordance with the memorial of Fiscal Commissioner-on-Staff, Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Chief of the Board Zeng Gongliang: 'When the court performs the ritual of suspending audiences, it is requested that audiences be suspended on the day after learning of the bereavement; those days of suspension shall count toward the total, and this shall serve as a permanent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Qingli (1045), the Board of Rites reported: "Pursuant to the memorial of Fiscal Commissioner Zeng Gongliang, Chief of the Board of Rites: 'When the court observes the ritual of suspending audiences upon a death, audiences should be suspended starting the day after word of bereavement arrives; those days should count toward the prescribed total, and this should be established as permanent precedent.

sentences.zh: 如值其日前殿須坐，則禮有重輕，自可略輕而為重，更不行輟朝之禮。

translations.literal: If it happens that on those days the front hall must be occupied for court, then since ritual has distinctions of greater and lesser weight, one may naturally set aside the lighter and perform the heavier, and further not carry out the ritual of suspending audiences.
translations.idiomatic: If on those days the main hall must be used for scheduled court business, ritual priority permits setting aside the lesser observance in favor of the greater, and the suspension need not be observed.'

sentences.zh: 』臣今看詳公亮所奏，誠於輟朝之間適宜順變。

translations.literal: ' Your servant has now examined Gongliang's memorial; it is indeed suitable and flexible in adapting the suspension of audiences.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed Gongliang's proposal and find it a reasonable and flexible adaptation of suspension protocol.

sentences.zh: 然慮君臣恩禮之情有所未盡，欲乞除人使見辭、春秋二宴合當舉樂，即於次日輟朝，餘乞依公亮所奏。

translations.literal: Yet we fear that the sentiments of grace and ritual between ruler and minister may not be fully expressed; we wish to request that except for audiences for envoys' farewells and the spring and autumn banquets when music ought properly to be performed, audiences be suspended on the following day; for the rest, we request compliance with Gongliang's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we fear this may not fully honor the bond of grace and ritual between sovereign and minister. We propose that except when envoys' farewell audiences or the spring and autumn banquets require music, suspension should begin the day after word arrives; in all other cases Gongliang's proposal should apply.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，守司空兼門下侍郎平章事薛居正薨，準禮，一品喪合輟二日，詔特輟三日。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, Defender of the Empty Quarter, Concurrent Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor Xue Juzheng died; according to ritual, mourning of first rank warranted suspension for two days; an edict specially suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo (981), Grand Councilor Xue Juzheng died; by regulation a first-rank death warranted two days' suspension, but an edict ordered a special three-day suspension.

sentences.zh: 其後鄧王錢俶、太師趙普、右僕射李沆薨，皆一品，合輟二日，詔並特輟五日。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Prince of Deng Qian Chu, Grand Preceptor Zhao Pu, and Right Vice Director of the Left Li Hang died—all first rank, requiring two days' suspension—edicts all specially suspended for five days.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Deng Qian Chu, Grand Preceptor Zhao Pu, and Vice Director Li Hang died—all first rank and normally entitled to two days—the court each time ordered special suspensions of five days.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品者，亦有特輟焉。

translations.literal: For second and third rank as well, there were special suspensions.
translations.idiomatic: Second- and third-rank officials also received special suspensions on occasion.

sentences.zh: 太平興國九年，右諫議大夫、參知政事李穆卒，準禮，諫議大夫不合輟朝，特輟一日。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo, Right Remonstrator and Participation Secretary Li Mu died; according to ritual, a Remonstrator did not warrant suspension of court; a special one-day suspension was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo (984), Participation Secretary Li Mu died; by regulation a Remonstrator did not qualify for suspended court, but the emperor ordered a special one-day suspension.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，羅彥瑰、魏仁浦薨，以郊祀及軍事不輟朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Luo Yankui and Wei Renpu died; because of suburban sacrifices and military affairs, court was not suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao (969), when Luo Yankui and Wei Renpu died, court was not suspended due to scheduled suburban sacrifices and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，同平章事王顯薨，以皇帝朝拜諸陵，吉凶難於相干，更不輟朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, Grand Councilor Wang Xian died; because the emperor was paying homage at the imperial tombs, auspicious and inauspicious matters were difficult to combine, and court was further not suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingde (1007), when Grand Councilor Wang Xian died, the emperor was paying homage at the imperial tombs; since auspicious and inauspicious rites could not easily coincide, court was not suspended.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，光祿卿鄭立卒，禮官舉故事輟朝，台官言：「卿、監職任疏遠，恩禮不稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, Director of Palace Supplies Zheng Li died; ritual officials cited precedent for suspension of court; censorial officials said: "Directors and commissioners hold distant responsibilities; the grace and ritual are not proportional.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangding (1040), when Director of Palace Supplies Zheng Li died, the Board of Rites invoked precedent for suspension; the censorate objected: "Directors and commissioners hold remote posts; their rank does not warrant such imperial honor.

sentences.zh: 」自後遂不輟朝。

translations.literal: " Thereafter court was no longer suspended.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter such deaths no longer triggered suspension of court.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道三年四月一日，太常寺言：「皇伯母秀王夫人薨，輟朝五日，內二日不視事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month in the third year of Qiandao during Emperor Xiaozong's reign, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "The emperor's grand-aunt, Lady of the Elegant Prince, has died; court is suspended for five days, within which two days the emperor does not hold audience for affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month of the third year of Qiandao (1167), the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "The emperor's grand-aunt-by-marriage, Lady of the Elegant Prince, has died. Court is to be suspended for five days, of which two days the emperor will not conduct state business.

sentences.zh: 乞自今月二日為始，輟朝至六日止，其二日、三日並不視事。

translations.literal: We request that from the second day of this month as the start, court be suspended until the sixth day, and on the second and third days the emperor likewise not hold audience for affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: We request suspension from the second of this month through the sixth, with the second and third days included among those when the emperor does not conduct state business.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 舉哀掛服。

translations.literal: Lamentation and donning mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Lamentation and Donning Mourning Dress.

sentences.zh: 尚舍設次於廣德殿或講武殿、大明殿，其後皆於後苑壬地。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Palace Supplies set up the venue at Guangde Hall, or Jiangwu Hall or Daming Hall; later all were at the ren site in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Palace Supplies prepared the venue at Guangde Hall, Jiangwu Hall, or Daming Hall; later all such ceremonies were held at the ren site in the rear imperial garden.

sentences.zh: 前一日，所司預設舉哀所幕殿，周以簾帷，色用青素。

translations.literal: On the preceding day, the responsible offices in advance set up a curtained hall as the site for lamentation, surrounded with curtains; the color used was green-black.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, the responsible offices erected a curtained mourning hall, draped with curtains in greenish-black.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝常服乘輿詣幕殿，侍臣奏 請降輿，俟時釋常服，服素服，白羅衫、黑銀腰帶、素紗軟腳襆頭。

translations.literal: On that day, the emperor in ordinary dress rode the imperial carriage to the curtained hall; attendant ministers memorialized requesting descent from the carriage; at the appointed time ordinary dress was removed and plain garments donned: white gauze shirt, black-silver belt, and plain gauze soft-footed headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor rode to the curtained hall in ordinary dress; attendants memorialized for him to alight, and at the appointed hour he changed into plain white mourning dress—a white gauze shirt, black-silver belt, and plain gauze soft-footed headwrap.

sentences.zh: 太常博士引太常卿當御坐前跪，奏請皇帝為某官薨舉哀，又請舉哭，十五舉音，又奏請可止。

translations.literal: A Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to kneel before the imperial seat, memorializing to request the emperor to lament the death of a certain official; again requesting the lamentation to begin; fifteen times the voice was raised; again memorializing that it might cease.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual doctor led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to kneel before the imperial seat and request the emperor to lament the death of the official in question; after requesting the lamentation, the emperor raised his voice fifteen times, whereupon the director memorialized that wailing might cease.

sentences.zh: 中 書、門下、文武百官進名於崇政殿門外奉慰。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs, the Chancellery, and civil and military officials of all ranks advanced with their names outside the Gate of Reverence for Governance to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Department of State Affairs, the Chancellery, and the civil and military bureaucracy registered their names outside the Gate of Reverence for Governance to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 皇帝釋素服，服常服，乘輿還內。

translations.literal: The emperor removed plain garments, donned ordinary dress, and rode the imperial carriage back within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed his mourning dress, resumed ordinary dress, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 真宗乳母秦國延壽保聖夫人卒，以太宗喪始期，疑舉哀，禮官言：「《通禮》：皇帝為乳母緦麻。

translations.literal: Wet nurse of Emperor Zhenzong, Lady of Qin State, Prolonged Life and Keeper of the Sacred Person, died; because the mourning for Emperor Taizong had just reached its first anniversary, there was doubt about performing lamentation; ritual officials said: "The Comprehensive Rites: the emperor wears sī mourning for a wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong's wet nurse, Lady of Qin, Prolonged Life and Keeper of the Sacred Person, died, the question arose whether to perform lamentation because Emperor Taizong's mourning period had only just reached its first anniversary. The Board of Rites cited the Comprehensive Rites: "The emperor wears coarse hemp mourning for a wet nurse."

sentences.zh: 按《喪葬令》：皇帝為緦，一舉哀止。

translations.literal: According to the Funeral Ordinances: for sī mourning, one lamentation and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Funeral Ordinances, sī-mourning requires only a single lamentation.

sentences.zh: 秦國夫人保傅聖躬，宜備哀榮。

translations.literal: The Lady of Qin State nurtured and tutored the Sacred Person; full lamentation and honor is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Qin had nurtured and tutored the emperor from infancy and deserved full mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 況太宗之喪已終易月之制，今為乳母發哀，合於禮典。

translations.literal: Moreover, mourning for Emperor Taizong had already completed the yi-month regulation; to perform lamentation now for the wet nurse conforms to ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the mourning period for Emperor Taizong had already passed its first anniversary; lamenting the wet nurse now accorded with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 康定二年，皇子壽國公昕薨，年二歲，禮官言：「已有爵命，宜同成人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangding, Imperial Prince Shouguo, Duke Xin, died at age two; ritual officials said: "He already held a title and rank; he should be treated the same as an adult.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangding, the two-year-old Imperial Prince Shouguo, Duke Xin, died. The Board of Rites held that because he had already received a title, he should be treated as an adult.

sentences.zh: 」遂發哀成服。

translations.literal: " Accordingly lamentation was performed and mourning garments donned.
translations.idiomatic: " Lamentation and full mourning dress followed.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，永國公薨，係無服之殤，詔特舉哀成服。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, Duke Yongguo died; he was an infant death without mourning obligation; an edict specially ordered lamentation and donning mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xining (1077), Duke Yongguo died as an infant requiring no mourning obligation, but an edict specially ordered lamentation and mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 輟樂。

translations.literal: Suspension of music.
translations.idiomatic: Suspension of Music.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年十 月，中書言：「今月七日乾明節，選定二十二日大宴。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, the Department of State Affairs reported: "On the seventh day of this month is the Qianming Festival; a great banquet has been set for the twenty-second day.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo (982), the Department of State Affairs reported: "The seventh of this month is the Qianming Festival, with a grand banquet scheduled for the twenty-second.

sentences.zh: 」二十日，參知政事竇偁卒，明日，皇帝親幸其第，臨喪慟哭，設奠還宮，即令罷宴。

translations.literal: " On the twentieth day, Participation Secretary Dou Cheng died; the next day the emperor personally visited his residence, attended the mourning and wailed in anguish, offered libations, returned to the palace, and immediately ordered the banquet cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twentieth, Participation Secretary Dou Cheng died. The next day the emperor visited his home in person, mourned at the bier, offered libations, and upon returning to the palace immediately ordered the banquet cancelled.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「伏以百司告 備，六樂在庭，睿聖至仁，聞哀而罷，是以顯君父愛慈之道，勵臣子忠孝之心。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized: "We respectfully note that all offices had reported readiness and the Six Musical Modes were in the hall; the sagely and benevolent sovereign, upon hearing of bereavement, cancelled the feast—thereby displaying the way of the ruler-father's love and compassion, and encouraging the hearts of ministers and sons in loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized: "All departments had completed preparations and the Six Musical Modes awaited performance in the hall. The sage and benevolent emperor, upon hearing of bereavement, cancelled the banquet—thereby exemplifying a ruler's compassionate love and inspiring loyalty and filial devotion among his ministers.

sentences.zh: 伏請宣付史館，傳錄美實。

translations.literal: We respectfully request that this be proclaimed and transmitted to the Historiography Office to record this fine deed.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully request that this be transmitted to the Historiography Office for recording.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 賻 贈。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts and grants.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral Gifts and Grants.

sentences.zh: 凡近臣及帶職事官薨，非詔葬者，如有喪訃及遷葬，皆賜賻贈，鴻臚寺與入內內侍省以舊例取旨。

translations.literal: Whenever close ministers and officials holding functional posts died, and it was not an imperially ordered funeral, if there was a report of death or reburial, funeral gifts and grants were all bestowed; the Court of State Ceremonial and the Inner Palace Service of the Inner Court followed old precedent to obtain imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a close minister or salaried official died without an imperially mandated funeral, funeral gifts were granted for death notices or reburials; the Court of State Ceremonial and the Inner Palace Service followed established precedent to obtain the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 其嘗踐兩府或任近侍者，多增其數，絹自五百匹至五十匹，錢 自五十萬至五萬，又賜羊酒有差，其優者仍給米麥香燭。

translations.literal: Those who had served in the two palaces or held close attendance had the amounts often increased: silk from five hundred bolts down to fifty, cash from five hundred thousand down to fifty thousand; sheep and wine were also granted in varying amounts, and for the most favored, rice, wheat, and incense candles were additionally supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had served in the executive or military palaces or as close attendants often received larger grants: silk ranging from five hundred to fifty bolts, cash from five hundred thousand to fifty thousand; sheep and wine were granted in graded amounts, with the most favored recipients additionally receiving rice, wheat, and incense candles.

sentences.zh: 自中書、樞密而下至兩省五品、三司三館職事、內職、軍校並執事禁近者亡歿，及父母、近親喪，皆有贈 賜。

translations.literal: From the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs down to fifth rank in the two departments, Three Departments and Three Academies functionaries, inner palace posts, and military officers, as well as those holding office close to the throne who died, and mourning for parents or close kin—all received grants.
translations.idiomatic: From the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs down to fifth rank in the two departments, plus functionaries of the Three Departments and Three Academies, inner palace personnel, military officers, and close attendants—deaths and mourning for parents or close kin all received grants.

sentences.zh: 宗室期、功、袒免、乳母、殤子及女出適者，各有常數。

translations.literal: Imperial clan members in qi, gong, and zan-mian relationships, wet nurses, infant deaths, and daughters married out—each had fixed amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen in various degrees of kinship, wet nurses, infant deaths, and daughters who had married out each received stipulated amounts.

sentences.zh: 其特恩加賜者，各以輕重為隆殺焉。

translations.literal: Those specially favored with additional grants were each graded by greater and lesser weight.
translations.idiomatic: Special additional grants were scaled according to the relative rank and relationship.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年十月，詔：「有死於矢石者，人給絹三匹，仍復其家三年，長吏存撫之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianlong, an edict: "Those who die from arrows and stones shall each be granted three bolts of silk; moreover their households shall be exempt from service for three years, and local magistrates shall provide care and support.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianlong (960), an edict declared: "Those who die in battle shall receive three bolts of silk each, and their households shall be exempt from corvée labor for three years, with local magistrates charged to provide care.

sentences.zh: 」慶曆二年，詔：「陣亡軍校無子孫者，賜其家錢，指揮使七萬，副指揮使六萬，軍使、都頭、副兵馬使、副都頭五萬。」

translations.literal: " In the second year of Qingli, an edict: "Military officers who died in battle without descendants—grant their households cash: commander seventy thousand, vice-commander sixty thousand, army commissioner, company chief, vice-cavalry commissioner, and vice-company chief fifty thousand each."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli (1042), an edict granted cash to the families of military officers killed in battle who left no descendants: seventy thousand for commanders, sixty thousand for vice-commanders, and fifty thousand for army commissioners, company chiefs, and their deputies.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年，參酌舊制著為新式：諸臣喪，兩人以上各該支賜孝贈，隻就數多者給；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining, old regulations were consulted and established as new format: for officials' mourning, when two or more persons each qualify for grants of mourning gifts, only the larger amount is granted;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xining (1074), existing regulations were codified into new rules: when two or more persons each qualify for funeral grants on an official's death, only the highest amount is paid;

sentences.zh: 官與職各該賻贈者，從多給，差遣、權並同，權發遣並與正同。

translations.literal: When both office and functional post each qualify for funeral gifts, the greater is granted; acting appointments and temporary appointments are treated the same, and temporary dispatch is treated the same as regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When both rank and functional title qualify for grants, the higher amount applies; acting and temporary appointments are treated the same as regular ones.

sentences.zh: 諸兩府、使相、 宣徽使並前任宰臣問疾或澆奠已賜不願敕葬者，並宗室不經澆奠支賜，雖不係敕葬，並支賻贈。

translations.literal: For all persons of the two palaces, envoys-in-chief, commissioners of the Palace Bureau, and former chief ministers to whom gifts were already granted for inquiry of illness or libation but who did not wish an imperially ordered funeral—and imperial clan members who did not receive grants through libation—all receive funeral gifts even though not subject to imperially ordered burial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilors, envoys-in-chief, palace commissioners, and former chief ministers who had received illness or libation gifts but declined an imperial funeral, as well as imperial clansmen who had not received libation grants—all received funeral gifts even without an imperial burial order.

sentences.zh: 餘但經問疾或澆奠支賜或敕葬者，更不支賻贈。

translations.literal: For the rest, those who only received grants for inquiry of illness or libation, or an imperially ordered funeral, receive no further funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: All others who had already received illness, libation, or imperial burial grants received no further funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 前兩府如澆奠隻支賻 贈，仍加絹一百、布一百、羊酒米麵各一十。

translations.literal: For former two-palace officials, if only libation grants were paid, funeral gifts are still granted, with an additional one hundred bolts of silk, one hundred bolts of cloth, and ten each of sheep, wine, rice, and flour.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand councilors who received only libation grants still received funeral gifts, plus an additional one hundred bolts of silk and cloth, and ten units each of sheep, wine, rice, and flour.

sentences.zh: 諸支賜孝贈：在京，羊每口支錢一貫，以折第二等絹充，每匹折錢一貫三百文，餘支本色；

translations.literal: For all grants of mourning gifts: in the capital, for each sheep cash of one string is granted, substituted with second-grade silk at one string three hundred cash per bolt; the rest is paid in kind;
translations.idiomatic: For funeral grants in the capital, each sheep was paid at one string of cash, convertible into second-grade silk at one string three hundred cash per bolt; other items were paid in kind;

sentences.zh: 在外，米支白秔米，麵每石 支小麥五斗，酒支細色，餘依價錢。
