translations.literal: Outside the capital, rice is granted as white polished rice; for flour, each picul grants five pecks of wheat; wine is granted as fine grade; the rest according to cash value.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital, rice was paid in polished white rice, flour at five pecks of wheat per picul, wine in fine grade, with other items paid at cash equivalent.

sentences.zh: 諸文臣卿監以上，武臣元係諸司使以上，分司、致仕身亡者，其賻贈並依見任官三分中給二，限百日內經所在官司投狀，召命官 保關申，限外不給。

translations.literal: For all civil officials of director rank and above, military officials originally holding commissioner rank and above, and those who died while serving remotely or in retirement—their funeral gifts are all granted at two-thirds of what active officials of the same rank receive; within one hundred days a petition must be submitted to the local office, with a named official guaranteeing the claim; beyond the limit, no grant.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of director rank and above, military officers of commissioner rank or higher, and officials who died while on detached service or in retirement received two-thirds of the grant payable to an active official of equivalent rank; claims had to be filed with the local office within one hundred days with a guarantor, or no payment was made.

sentences.zh: 待制、觀察使以上更不召保。

translations.literal: For stewards of the Academy and observation commissioners and above, no guarantor need be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards of the Academy and observation commissioners and above were exempt from the guarantor requirement.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，詔：「鄜延路沒於王事、有家屬見今在本路欲歸鄉者給賻外，其大使臣以上更支行李錢百千，小使臣五十千，差使、殿侍三十千，其餘比類支給。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict: "For those on the Fuyan Circuit who died in service to the state and whose families presently in that circuit wish to return home—in addition to funeral grants, for great envoys and above an additional one hundred thousand cash for travel expenses, for minor envoys fifty thousand, for dispatch envoys and palace attendants thirty thousand; others by comparable grant."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng (1082), an edict stated: "For those on the Fuyan Circuit who died in the state's service whose families wish to return home, in addition to funeral grants, great envoys and above receive an extra one hundred thousand cash for travel expenses, minor envoys fifty thousand, and dispatch envoys and palace attendants thirty thousand, with comparable amounts for others."

sentences.zh: 紹興二十六年，詔：「今後命官實因幹辦公事邂逅非理致死者，並遵依舊法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing, an edict: "From now on, when appointed officials truly die unexpectedly and by violence while handling public business, all follow the old law.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing (1156), an edict declared: "Hereafter, when appointed officials die unexpectedly by accident or violence while handling public business, the old law shall apply.

sentences.zh: 所有李光申請於《紹興條》內添注日限指揮，更不施行。

translations.literal: The request by Li Guang to add a time-limit directive within the Shaoxing regulations shall no longer be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang's proposal to add a time-limit provision to the Shaoxing regulations shall no longer apply.

sentences.zh: 」舊法非理致死者，謂焚溺 墜壓之類，通判以上賜銀五百兩，餘三百兩，職司已上取旨。

translations.literal: " The old law for deaths by violence refers to burning, drowning, falls, crushing, and the like: prefectural judges and above receive five hundred taels of silver, the rest three hundred taels; functional commissioners and above receive grants according to imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The old law defined accidental violent death as burning, drowning, falls, crushing, and the like: officials of prefectural judge rank and above received five hundred taels of silver, others three hundred; functional commissioners and above received grants at imperial discretion.

sentences.zh: 初，紹興二年五月，吏部侍郎李光申明立定折跌骨五十餘日，三十日內身亡之人，並支前項銀數。

translations.literal: Initially, in the fifth month of the second year of Shaoxing, Vice Director of Personnel Li Guang clarified that for fall injuries with bone fractures of fifty-odd days' duration, persons who died within thirty days all received the aforesaid silver amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Shaoxing (1132), Vice Director of Personnel Li Guang had ruled that persons who died within thirty days of a bone fracture from a fall sustained more than fifty days earlier qualified for the prescribed silver grant.

sentences.zh: 至 是，戶部侍郎宋貺言：「自立定日限，後來多是因他病身故之人，子孫規圖賞給，計會所屬，旋作差出名目，陳乞保奏，誠為期罔。

translations.literal: At this time, Vice Director of Revenue Song Kuang said: "Since the time limit was established, most cases afterward have been persons who died from other illnesses; descendants schemed for the reward grant, colluded with responsible offices, quickly fabricated nominal assignments, and submitted petitions with guarantors—this is truly deceit.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Vice Director of Revenue Song Kuang reported: "Since that time limit was established, most claims have involved persons who died of unrelated illnesses; descendants schemed for the reward, colluded with local officials, fabricated nominal assignments, and submitted fraudulent petitions—a clear abuse.

sentences.zh: 」故有是命。

translations.literal: " Hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence the present edict.

sentences.zh: 詔 葬。

translations.literal: Imperially ordered funerals.
translations.idiomatic: Imperially Ordered Funerals.

sentences.zh: 《禮院例冊》：諸一品、二品喪，敕備本品鹵簿送葬者，以少牢贈祭於都城外，加璧，束帛深青二、纁二。

translations.literal: Board of Rites precedent records: for all mourning of first and second rank, when an edict orders the full insignia escort of that rank to accompany the funeral, a shaolao offering is presented outside the capital city, with added jade bi, two bundles of dark green silk and two bundles of russet silk.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Board of Rites precedent records, for first- and second-rank deaths when an edict ordered the deceased's full rank insignia to escort the funeral, a shaolao offering was presented outside the capital, with an added jade bi and bundles of dark green and russet silk.

sentences.zh: 諸重：一品柱鬲六，五品已上四，六品已下二。

translations.literal: For all bell frames: first rank six pole-frames and tripods; fifth rank and above four; sixth rank and below two.
translations.idiomatic: Bell frames: first rank, six pole-stands with tripods; fifth rank and above, four; sixth rank and below, two.

sentences.zh: 諸銘 旌：三品已上長九尺，五品已上八尺，六品已上七尺，皆書某官封姓之柩。

translations.literal: For all inscription banners: third rank and above, nine feet long; fifth rank and above, eight feet; sixth rank and above, seven feet; all inscribed "Coffin of [title] [surname]."
translations.idiomatic: Inscription banners: third rank and above, nine feet; fifth rank and above, eight feet; sixth rank and above, seven feet—all inscribed with the deceased's title and surname.

sentences.zh: 諸而車：三品已上油幰、牛絲絡綱施襈，兩廂畫龍，幰竿諸末垂六旒蘇；

translations.literal: For all funeral carriages: third rank and above, oiled canopy, ox with silk net, rope with hanging pennants, both sides painted with dragons, canopy pole tips with six tassel clusters;
translations.idiomatic: Funeral carriages: third rank and above had oiled canopies, oxen with silk trappings, rope pennants, dragon paintings on both sides, and six tassel clusters hanging from the canopy poles;

sentences.zh: 七品已上油幰、 施襈，兩廂畫雲氣，垂四旒蘇；

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above, oiled canopy and hanging pennants, both sides painted with cloud patterns, four tassel clusters;
translations.idiomatic: seventh rank and above had oiled canopies and pennants, cloud patterns on both sides, and four tassel clusters;

sentences.zh: 九品已上無旒蘇；

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above, no tassel clusters;
translations.idiomatic: ninth rank and above had no tassel clusters;

sentences.zh: 庶人鱉甲車，無幰、巽、畫飾。

translations.literal: Commoners use tortoise-shell-pattern carts, without canopy, awning, or painted decoration.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners used plain tortoise-pattern carts without canopy, awning, or painted decoration.

sentences.zh: 諸引、披、鐸、翣、輓歌：三品已上四引、四披、六鐸、六翣、輓歌六行三十六 人；

translations.literal: For all guides, mantle-bearers, bells, feather-fans, and dirge singers: third rank and above, four guides, four mantle-bearers, six bells, six feather-fans, six rows of dirge singers totaling thirty-six persons;
translations.idiomatic: Guides, mantle-bearers, bells, feather-fans, and dirge singers: third rank and above, four guides, four mantle-bearers, six bells, six feather-fans, and six rows totaling thirty-six dirge singers;

sentences.zh: 四品二引、二披、四鐸、四翣、輓歌者四行十六人；

translations.literal: Fourth rank, two guides, two mantle-bearers, four bells, four feather-fans, four rows of dirge singers totaling sixteen persons;
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank, two guides, two mantle-bearers, four bells, four feather-fans, and sixteen dirge singers in four rows;

sentences.zh: 五品、六品輓歌八人；

translations.literal: Fifth and sixth rank, eight dirge singers;
translations.idiomatic: fifth and sixth rank, eight dirge singers;

sentences.zh: 七品、八品輓歌六人；

translations.literal: Seventh and eighth rank, six dirge singers;
translations.idiomatic: seventh and eighth rank, six dirge singers;

sentences.zh: 六品、九品

translations.literal: Sixth rank, ninth rank
translations.idiomatic: sixth and ninth ranks—

sentences.zh: （謂非升朝者）〉

translations.literal: (meaning those not attending court)
translations.idiomatic: (meaning those not in court audience)

sentences.zh: 輓歌四人。

translations.literal: Dirge singers, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Four dirge singers.

sentences.zh: 其持引、披者，皆布 幘、布深衣；

translations.literal: Those who hold the guide ropes and pall all wear cloth turbans and cloth deep garments;
translations.idiomatic: Those bearing the guide ropes and pall all wear cloth turbans and plain hemp deep robes;

sentences.zh: 輓歌，白練幘、白練褠衣，皆執鐸、綍，並鞋襪。

translations.literal: Dirge singers wear white silk turbans and white silk padded garments, all hold bells and mourning cords, with shoes and socks.
translations.idiomatic: Dirge singers wear white silk turbans and padded white silk robes, carry bells and mourning ropes, and wear shoes and stockings.

sentences.zh: 諸四品已上用方相，七品已上用魌頭。

translations.literal: For all: fourth rank and above use fangxiang exorcists; seventh rank and above use qi tou demon masks.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and above used fangxiang exorcists; seventh rank and above used demon-mask bearers.

sentences.zh: 諸纛：五品已上，其竿長九尺；

translations.literal: For all funeral banners: fifth rank and above, the pole is nine feet long;
translations.idiomatic: Funeral banners: fifth rank and above, poles nine feet long;

sentences.zh: 已下五尺已上。

translations.literal: Below that, five feet and above.
translations.idiomatic: below that, from five feet upward.

sentences.zh: 諸葬不得以石 為棺槨及石室，其棺槨皆不得雕鏤彩畫、施方牖檻，棺內不得藏金寶珠玉。

translations.literal: For all burials, one may not use stone for coffin and outer coffin or stone chambers; the coffin and outer coffin may not be carved, inlaid, painted in colors, or fitted with square latticed windows and railings; within the coffin one may not store gold, treasure, pearls, or jade.
translations.idiomatic: Burials may not use stone coffins, outer coffins, or stone chambers; coffins may not be carved, painted, or fitted with latticed windows and railings; and no gold, jewels, pearls, or jade may be placed within.

sentences.zh: 又按《會要》：勳戚大臣薨卒，多命詔葬，遣中使監護，官給其費，以表一 時之恩。

translations.literal: Again according to the Institutional Compendium: when meritorious kin and great ministers died, imperial burial was often ordered, palace envoys were dispatched to supervise, and the state supplied the costs, thereby displaying a timely favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Institutional Compendium also records that when meritorious imperial kin or great ministers died, an imperial funeral was often ordered, a palace envoy dispatched to supervise, and the costs paid by the state—a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 凡凶儀皆有買道、方相、引魂車，香、蓋、紙錢、鵝毛、影輿，錦繡虛車，大輿，銘旌；

translations.literal: All inauspicious rites have way-purchasing, fangxiang exorcists, soul-guiding carriages, incense, canopies, paper money, goose feathers, spirit-image palanquins, brocade-decorated empty carriages, great carriages, and inscription banners;
translations.idiomatic: All state funeral regalia included way-purchasing rites, fangxiang exorcists, soul-guiding carriages, incense, canopies, paper money, goose-feather banners, spirit-image palanquins, brocade dummy carriages, the main hearse, and inscription banners;

sentences.zh: 儀棺，行幕，各一；

translations.literal: Ceremonial coffin and traveling canopy, one each;
translations.idiomatic: a ceremonial coffin and a traveling canopy, one each;

sentences.zh: 輓歌十六。

translations.literal: Sixteen dirge singers.
translations.idiomatic: sixteen dirge singers.

sentences.zh: 其明器、床帳、衣輿、結彩床皆不 定數。

translations.literal: Spirit objects, bed curtains, clothing palanquins, and decorated mourning beds all have no fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit goods, bed curtains, clothing palanquins, and decorated mourning beds had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 墳所有石羊虎、望柱各二，三品以上加石人二人。

translations.literal: At the grave site: stone sheep and tigers, and sight pillars, two each; third rank and above add two stone human figures.
translations.idiomatic: The grave precinct had two stone sheep, two stone tigers, and two sight pillars; third rank and above added two stone human figures.

sentences.zh: 入墳有當壙、當野、祖思、祖明、地軸、十二時神、誌石、券石、鐵券各一。

translations.literal: Entering the grave: dangkuang, dangye, Zusi, Zuming, earth axis, twelve time spirits, epitaph stone, contract stone, and iron contract, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Burial rites included one each of the tomb-sealing, open-field, Zusi, and Zuming ceremonies, the earth-axis effigy, the twelve time spirits, epitaph stone, contract stone, and iron deed.

sentences.zh: 殯前一日對靈柩，及至墳所下 事時，皆設敕祭，監葬官行禮。

translations.literal: One day before encoffining, facing the spirit coffin, and when completing the burial at the grave site, imperial sacrifices were all set up, and the burial-supervising officer performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before encoffining, when facing the coffin, and again when completing burial at the grave, imperial sacrifices were performed by the supervising burial officer.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，又著新式，頒於有司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, new formats were again established and issued to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reign (1068–1077), new regulations were compiled and promulgated to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年六月，中書令、秦國公孟昶薨，其母李氏繼亡，命鴻臚範禹偁監護喪事，仍詔 禮官議定吉凶儀仗禮例以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Qiande, Meng Chang, Grand Councillor and Duke of Qin State, died; his mother Lady Li died shortly afterward; Fan Yucheng of the Court of State Ceremonial was ordered to supervise the funeral; still an edict ordered ritual officials to deliberate and fix the precedents for auspicious and inauspicious guards and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Qiande (965), Meng Chang, Chief Councillor and Duke of Qin, died; his mother Lady Li soon followed. Fan Yucheng of the Court of State Ceremonial was appointed to supervise the funeral, and ritual officials were ordered to determine the funeral protocol and report.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「檢詳故事，晉天福十二年葬故魏王，周廣順元年葬故樞密使楊邠、侍衛使史弘肇、三司使王章例，並用一品禮。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Upon examining precedents: in the twelfth year of Tianfu of Jin, burial of the late King of Wei; in the first year of Guangshun of Zhou, burial of the late commissioner of the Military Affairs Bureau Yang Bin, commissioner of the Guard Bureau Shi Hongzhao, and commissioner of the Three Departments Bureau Wang Zhang—all used first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ritual reported: "Examining precedents, the burials of the late King of Wei in Jin Tianfu 12 (947), and of Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Wang Zhang in Later Zhou Guangshun 1 (951)—all used first-rank funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 墓方圓 九十步，墳高一丈八尺，明器九十事，石作六事，音身隊二十人，當壙、當野、祖明、祖思、地軸、十二時神、蚊廚帳、暖帳各一，需車一，輓歌三十六人；

translations.literal: The grave square and round ninety paces; mound height one zhang eight chi; spirit objects ninety items; stone works six items; musical escort detachment twenty persons; dangkuang, dangye, Zuming, Zusi, earth axis, twelve time spirits, mosquito-kitchen canopy, warm canopy each one; supply carriage one; dirge singers thirty-six persons;
translations.idiomatic: The grave measured ninety paces square; the mound stood one zhang eight chi; there were ninety spirit objects, six stone works, and a twenty-man musical escort; one each of the tomb-sealing, open-field, Zuming, Zusi, earth-axis, twelve time spirits, mosquito-kitchen, and warm canopies; one supply carriage; and thirty-six dirge singers;

sentences.zh: 拂一、 纛一、翣六、盾車、魂車、儀槨車、買道車、誌石車各一；

translations.literal: One whisk, one banner, six feather fans, shield carriage, soul carriage, ceremonial coffin carriage, way-purchasing carriage, epitaph carriage, each one;
translations.idiomatic: one whisk, one banner, six feather fans, and one each of the shield carriage, soul carriage, ceremonial coffin carriage, way-purchasing carriage, and epitaph carriage;

sentences.zh: 方相氏、鵝毛纛、銘旌、香輿、影輿、蓋輿、錢輿、五穀輿、酒醢輿、衣物輿、庖牲輿各一；

translations.literal: Fangxiang exorcist, goose-feather banner, inscription banner, incense palanquin, spirit-image palanquin, canopy palanquin, money palanquin, five-grain palanquin, wine-and-saltmeat palanquin, clothing palanquin, kitchen-sacrifice palanquin, each one;
translations.idiomatic: one fangxiang exorcist, goose-feather banner, inscription banner, and one each of the incense, spirit-image, canopy, paper-money, grain, wine-and-preserves, clothing, and kitchen-offering palanquins;

sentences.zh: 黃白紙帳、 園宅、象生什物、行幕，並誌文、輓歌詞、啟攢啟奠祝文，並請下有司修製。

translations.literal: Yellow and white paper canopies, estate models, lifelike assorted objects, traveling canopies, together with epitaph text, dirge lyrics, coffin-opening and libation prayer texts—all requested to be sent down to relevant offices for preparation.
translations.idiomatic: They requested that relevant offices prepare yellow and white paper canopies, estate models, lifelike grave goods, traveling tents, the epitaph, dirge lyrics, and the coffin-opening and libation prayers.

sentences.zh: 其儀：太僕寺革輅，兵部本品鹵簿儀仗，太常寺本品鼓吹儀仗，殿中省傘一、曲蓋二、 朱漆團扇四，自第導引出城，量遠近各還。

translations.literal: The ceremony: the Court of the Imperial Stud supplied the leather chariot; the Ministry of War, this rank's guard regalia; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, this rank's drum-and-pipe guard; the Palace Domestic Service one umbrella, two curved canopies, four vermilion-lacquered round fans; from the residence as escort out of the city, according to distance each returned.
translations.idiomatic: The procession would include the Court of the Imperial Stud's leather chariot, this rank's guard regalia from the Ministry of War, and matching musical escort from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the Palace Domestic Service would supply one umbrella, two curved canopies, and four vermilion round fans; these would escort the cortege from the residence out of the city and return according to distance.

sentences.zh: 贈玉一、纁二，贈祭少牢禮料，亦請下光祿、太府寺、少府監諸司依禮供應。

translations.literal: Grant jade one, hsien two; grant sacrifice young ox feast ritual supplies; also request to send down to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Treasury, Directorate of the Palace Domestic Service and other offices to supply according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: One jade tablet and two bolts of hsien silk were to be granted, along with a young-ox sacrificial feast; the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Treasury, and Directorate of the Palace Domestic Service were requested to supply these according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 又楚王母依子官一品例，準令文，外命婦一 品侍近二人、青衣六人，偏扇、方扇各十六，行鄣三、坐鄣二，白銅飾犢車駕牛馭人四，從人十六，夾車、從車六，傘一、大扇一、團扇二、戟六十。

translations.literal: Also the Chu king's mother, following her son's first-rank precedent, per the statute text: exterior enfeoffed consort of first rank—attendants near at hand two persons, green-robed attendants six persons; side fans and square fans sixteen each; traveling screens three, sitting screens two; white-copper-decorated calf carriage drawn by four ox handlers; followers sixteen; flanking carriages and attendant carriages six; umbrella one, large fan one, round fans two, halberds sixty.
translations.idiomatic: For Meng Chang's mother, following her son's first-rank status, the regulations called for a first-rank enfeoffed lady: two close attendants, six green-robed maidservants, sixteen side fans and sixteen square fans, three traveling screens and two sitting screens, a white-copper-decorated calf carriage with four handlers, sixteen followers, six flanking and escort carriages, one umbrella, one large fan, two round fans, and sixty halberds.

sentences.zh: 伏緣久不施 用，如特賜施行，即合於孟昶吉凶仗內相參排列。

translations.literal: Your humble [servants] submit that these have long gone unused; if specially granted for implementation, they should be arranged in coordination within Meng Chang's auspicious and inauspicious guards.
translations.idiomatic: These items had long fallen out of use; if specially granted for this occasion, they should be incorporated into Meng Chang's funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 」詔並令排列祗應，仍俟導引至城外，分半導至西京墳下及葬，命供奉官周貽慶押奉議軍士二指揮防護至洛陽。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered all arranged to serve; still awaited escort to outside the city, then half escorted to the grave site at Western Capital and burial; ordered palace attendant Zhou Yiqing to lead two commands of Fengyi Army soldiers to escort as guard to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all items prepared and deployed; after escorting the cortege outside the city, half the escort would continue to the Western Capital grave for burial. Palace attendant Zhou Yiqing was ordered to lead two commands of Fengyi Army soldiers as guard escort to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 又 賜子玄喆墳莊一區。

translations.literal: Also granted his son Xuanzhe one burial estate parcel.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang's son Xuanzhe was also granted a burial estate.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，建武軍節度使何繼筠卒，詔遣中使護葬，仍賜寶劍、甲胄同葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, He Jiyun, military commissioner of Jianwu Army, died; an edict dispatched a palace envoy to oversee the burial, still granting a treasured sword and armor to be buried with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao (971), He Jiyun, military commissioner of Jianwu, died; a palace envoy was dispatched to supervise the burial, and a treasured sword and suit of armor were granted for burial with him.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，護國軍節度使、駙馬都尉王承衍葬，鹵簿、 鼓吹備而不作，以在太宗大祥忌禁內也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, burial of Wang Chengyan, military commissioner of Huguo Army and imperial son-in-law; guard regalia and drum-and-pipe music were prepared but not performed, because it was within the second-anniversary mourning prohibition for Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping (998), at the burial of Wang Chengyan, military commissioner of Huguo and imperial son-in-law, guard regalia and musical escort were assembled but not performed, as the occasion fell within the second-anniversary mourning restrictions for Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，崇信軍節度使、華陰郡王宗旦薨，聽以旌節、牌印葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, Zong Dan, military commissioner of Chongxin Army and Prince of Huayin, died; permission was granted to bury his command baton and seal plaque with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng (1082), Zong Dan, Prince of Huayin and military commissioner of Chongxin, died; he was permitted to be buried with his command baton and seal of office.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔：不即隨葬者徒二年，因而行用者罪之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward another edict: those who do not immediately bury them with the deceased are penalized two years' penal servitude; those who put them to use are punished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon followed: failure to bury them immediately with the deceased was punishable by two years' penal servitude; unauthorized use was also a punishable offense.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十 四年，太師、清河郡王張俊葬，上曰：「張俊極宣力，與他將不同，恩數務從優厚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, burial of Zhang Jun, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Qinghe; the emperor said: "Zhang Jun exerted himself to the utmost; unlike other generals—favors should be made especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing (1154), at the burial of Zhang Jun, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Qinghe, the emperor said: "Zhang Jun served with exceptional zeal, unlike other generals; his honors should be especially generous.

sentences.zh: 」仍賜七梁額花冠貂蟬籠巾朝服一襲、水銀二百兩、龍腦一百五十兩。

translations.literal: " Still granted one set of seven-ridge floriated headdress, marten-and-cicada official cap, wrapped cap, and court robe; two hundred taels of mercury; one hundred fifty taels of borneol.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted a full set of court dress including a seven-ridge floriated crown and marten-trimmed cap, two hundred taels of mercury, and one hundred fifty taels of borneol.

sentences.zh: 其後，楊 存中薨，孝宗令諸寺院聲鍾，仍賜水銀、龍腦以斂。

translations.literal: Afterward, Yang Cunzhong died; Emperor Xiaozong ordered temples to sound bells, still granting mercury and borneol for encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yang Cunzhong died, Emperor Xiaozong ordered temples to toll their bells and granted mercury and borneol for the encoffining.

sentences.zh: 《熙寧新式》：先是，知制誥曾布言：「竊以朝廷親睦九族，故於死喪之際，臨吊賻恤，至於窀穸 之具，皆給於縣官，又擇近臣專董其事，所以深致其哀榮而盡其送終之禮。

translations.literal: New Format of Xining: earlier, Drafting Edict Officer Zeng Bu said: "Your servant submits that the court cherishes kinship with the nine clans; therefore at death and mourning, attending to offer condolences and funeral gifts, even to burial goods—all are supplied by the state; moreover close ministers are chosen to oversee the matter exclusively, thereby deeply conferring mourning honor and fully completing the rites of seeing off the dead.
translations.idiomatic: New Format of Xining: Drafting Edict Officer Zeng Bu had earlier observed: "The court cherishes its imperial kin; at death it sends condolences and funeral gifts, supplies burial goods at state expense, and appoints close ministers to oversee the arrangements—all to confer full mourning honor and complete the rites of seeing off the dead.

sentences.zh: 近世使臣沿襲故常，過取饋遺，故私家之費，往往倍於公上。

translations.literal: In recent times envoys followed old custom and excessively accepted gifts; thus private household costs often doubled those from the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times, however, envoys had followed old custom and accepted excessive gifts, so private costs often doubled the state's expenditure.

sentences.zh: 祥符中，患其無節，嘗詔有 司定其數。

translations.literal: In Xiangfu, concerned at the lack of restraint, an edict once ordered relevant offices to fix the amounts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiangfu era (1008–1016), concerned at the lack of restraint, the court once ordered relevant offices to fix the amounts.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，又著之《編敕》，令使臣所受無過五百，朝臣無過三百，有違之者，御史奏劾。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, it was again entered in the Compiled Statutes, ordering that envoys receive no more than five hundred, court ministers no more than three hundred; violators were impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangyou era (1049–1053), limits were codified in the Compiled Statutes: envoys could accept no more than five hundred, court ministers no more than three hundred; violators were subject to censorial impeachment.

sentences.zh: 伏見比歲以來，不復循守，其取之者不啻十倍於著令。

translations.literal: Your humble [servants] observe that in recent years these are no longer followed; what is taken is not merely ten times the stipulated regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, however, these limits have gone unenforced; what envoys accept is often ten times the stipulated amount.

sentences.zh: 乞取舊例 裁定酌中之數，以為永式。

translations.literal: Your servant requests taking old precedents to fix a measured moderate amount as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: I request that old precedents be consulted to establish a moderate fixed amount as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 」詔令太常禮院詳定，令布裁定以聞。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine and fix it, ordering Bu to fix it and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Directorate of Ritual to review the matter and directed Zeng Bu to determine the amounts and report.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐七年，詔大宗正：自今皇親之喪，五年以上未葬者，不以有無尊親新喪，並擇日 葬之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiayou, an edict to the Director of the Imperial Clan: from now on, for imperial kin's mourning, those unburied five years or more—regardless of whether there is a senior relative's new mourning—all choose a day and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiayou (1062), the Director of the Imperial Clan was ordered: henceforth, any imperial kinsman's remains unburied for five years or more were to be buried on a chosen day, regardless of whether a senior relative had recently died.

sentences.zh: 初，龍圖閣直學士向傳式言：「故事，皇親係節度使以上方許承凶營葬，其卑幼喪皆隨葬之。

translations.literal: Initially, Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams Xiang Chuanshi said: "By precedent, imperial kin of military commissioner rank and above were permitted to undertake mourning and arrange burial; the deaths of younger and junior kin were all buried along with them.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a memorial by Xiang Chuanshi, Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams: "By precedent, only imperial kin of military commissioner rank or above could undertake mourning and arrange burial; the deaths of younger and junior kin were buried along with them.

sentences.zh: 自慶曆八年後，積十二年未葬者幾四百餘喪，官司難於卒辦，致 濮王薨百日不及葬。

translations.literal: From after the eighth year of Qingli, accumulated over twelve years, nearly four hundred or more unburied deaths; the offices found it hard to complete at once, causing the Prince of Pu, upon death, not to reach burial within one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Since the eighth year of Qingli (1048), nearly four hundred deaths had accumulated unburied over twelve years; the bureaucracy could not cope, with the result that when the Prince of Pu died, burial could not be completed within the hundred-day mourning period.

sentences.zh: 請自今兩宅遇有尊屬之喪，不以官品為限而葬之。

translations.literal: Your servant requests that from now on, when the two residences encounter mourning for senior kin, without limit of official rank, bury them.
translations.idiomatic: I request that henceforth, whenever either imperial residence suffers the death of a senior relative, burial proceed without regard to official rank.

sentences.zh: 」下判大宗正司、太常禮儀院、司天監議，而有是詔。

translations.literal: " It was sent down for deliberation to the Imperial Clan Directorate, the Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the Directorate of Astronomy, and there was this edict.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Imperial Clan Directorate, the Directorate of Ritual, and the Directorate of Astronomy for deliberation, resulting in this edict.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，又詔御史臺：「臣僚父母無故 十年不葬，即依條彈奏，及令吏部候限滿檢察。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou, another edict to the Censorate: "When officials' parents are without cause unburied for ten years, immediately impeach according to the statute, and order the Ministry of Personnel, when the term expires, to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era (1086–1094), the Censorate was further ordered: "When an official's parents remain unburied without cause for ten years, impeach according to statute, and direct the Ministry of Personnel to inspect when the term expires.

sentences.zh: 尚有不葬父母，即未得與關升磨勘。

translations.literal: If parents are still unburied, one may not participate in promotion and merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Officials whose parents remain unburied may not be considered for promotion or merit review.

sentences.zh: 如失檢察，亦許彈奏。」

translations.literal: If inspection is missed, impeachment is also permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Failure to inspect may also be impeached."

sentences.zh: 追封冊命。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffment and patent.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous Enfeoffment and Patent.

sentences.zh: 《通禮》：策贈貴臣，守宮於主人大門外設使、副位，使人公服從朝堂受策，載於犢車，各備鹵簿，至主人之門降車。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Rites: when bestowing patents on honored ministers posthumously, the palace attendant sets chief and deputy envoy positions outside the host's main gate; envoys in official dress receive the patent from the court hall, load it on a calf carriage, each equipped with guard regalia, and at the host's gate descend from the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites stipulates that for posthumous enfeoffment of honored ministers, palace attendants set up chief and deputy envoy positions outside the bereaved family's main gate; envoys in official dress receive the patent at court, load it on a calf carriage with full guard regalia, and dismount at the family's gate.

sentences.zh: 使者稱：「有制。

translations.literal: The envoy announces: "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy announces: "By imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 」主人降階稽顙，內外皆哭。

translations.literal: " The host descends the steps and prostrates; inner and outer all weep.
translations.idiomatic: The bereaved family descends the steps and prostrates; all within and without weep.

sentences.zh: 讀冊訖，主人拜送之。

translations.literal: When reading the patent is finished, the host bows and sees them off.
translations.idiomatic: After the patent is read, the host bows and sees the envoys off.

sentences.zh: 定諡。

translations.literal: Fixing posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Fixing Posthumous Titles.

sentences.zh: 王公及職事官三品以上薨

translations.literal: When princes and functional officials of third rank and above die
translations.idiomatic: When princes and salaried officials of third rank and above die—

sentences.zh: （贈官同）〉

translations.literal: (meaning same as posthumously conferred rank)
translations.idiomatic: (meaning same as posthumously conferred rank)

sentences.zh: ，本家錄行狀上尚書省，考功移太常禮院議定，博士撰議，考功審覆，判都省集合省官參議，具上中書門下宰臣判準， 始錄奏聞。

translations.literal: , the household records a conduct summary and submits it to the Department of State Affairs; the Directorate of Merit Review transfers it to the Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation and fixing; the academician drafts the evaluation; the Directorate of Merit Review examines and reviews; the chief of the Department assembles provincial officials for joint deliberation; submits complete report to the Secretariat-Chancellery for chief ministers' approval; only then records and memorializes to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: the family submits a conduct summary to the Department of State Affairs; the Directorate of Merit Review forwards it to the Directorate of Ritual for deliberation; a ritual academician drafts the evaluation; the Directorate of Merit Review reviews it; the chief of the Department convenes provincial officials for joint deliberation; and upon approval by the chief ministers, the posthumous title is recorded and memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 敕付所司即考功錄牒，以未葬前賜其家。

translations.literal: An edict is delivered to the relevant office, and immediately the Directorate of Merit Review records the patent, granting it to the family before burial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directs the relevant office to record the patent, which the Directorate of Merit Review grants to the family before burial.

sentences.zh: 省官有異議者，聽具議聞。

translations.literal: If provincial officials have differing views, they are permitted to submit their views and report.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials who dissent may submit their views for report.

sentences.zh: 蘊德丘園，聲實明著，雖無官爵，亦奏賜諡曰「先生」。

translations.literal: Those who store virtue in hills and gardens, whose reputation and substance are clearly distinguished—even without office or rank—are also memorialized and granted the posthumous title "Master."
translations.idiomatic: Those of distinguished virtue and reputation who lived in retirement—even without office or rank—might also be granted the posthumous title "Master."

sentences.zh: 太平興國八 年，詔增《周公諡法》五十五字，美諡七十一字為一百字，平諡七字為二十字，惡諡十七字為三十字。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict added fifty-five characters to the Duke of Zhou's Posthumous Title Canon; laudatory titles from seventy-one characters to one hundred; neutral titles from seven characters to twenty; pejorative titles from seventeen characters to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo (983), the Duke of Zhou's Posthumous Title Canon was expanded by fifty-five characters: laudatory titles from seventy-one to one hundred, neutral titles from seven to twenty, and pejorative titles from seventeen to thirty.

sentences.zh: 其沈約、賀琛《續廣諡》盡廢。

translations.literal: Shen Yue's and He Chen's Continued and Expanded Posthumous Titles were entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue's and He Chen's Continued and Expanded Posthumous Titles were entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 後以直史館胡旦言：「舊制， 文武官臣僚皆以功行上下，各賜諡法。

translations.literal: Later, based on the words of Hanlin Compiler Hu Dan: "By old regulation, civil and military officials and ministers all, according to merit and conduct high and low, each received posthumous title canons.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Hanlin Compiler Hu Dan observed: "Under the old system, civil and military officials received posthumous title canons according to their merit and conduct.

sentences.zh: 近朝以來，遂成闕典。

translations.literal: In recent courts, this has become a missing institution.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times this practice had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 建隆以後，臣僚三品以上合賜諡者百餘人，望令史館編錄行狀，送禮官定諡付館，修入國史。

translations.literal: Since Jianlong, more than one hundred officials of third rank and above who should receive posthumous titles—your servant hopes to order the Historiography Institute to compile and record conduct summaries, send them to ritual officials to fix posthumous titles and deliver to the institute, and enter them in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jianlong era (960–963), more than one hundred officials of third rank and above who should have received posthumous titles had not; I request that the Historiography Institute compile their conduct summaries, send them to ritual officials to fix posthumous titles, and enter them in the national history.

sentences.zh: 」詔：「 今後並令禮官取行狀定諡，送考功詳覆，關送史館，永為定式。」

translations.literal: " An edict: "From now on, all order ritual officials to take conduct summaries and fix posthumous titles, send to the Directorate of Merit Review for detailed review, transmit to the Historiography Institute, permanently as fixed standard."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Henceforth ritual officials shall determine posthumous titles from conduct summaries, submit them to the Directorate of Merit Review for review, and transmit them to the Historiography Institute—this shall be the permanent standard."

sentences.zh: 直集賢院王皞言：「諡者，行之表也。

translations.literal: Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Excellence Wang Hao said: "A posthumous title is the outward expression of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao, Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Excellence, argued: "A posthumous title is the outward expression of a person's conduct.

sentences.zh: 善行有善諡，惡行有惡諡，蓋聞諡知行，以為 勸戒。

translations.literal: Good conduct has good posthumous titles, evil conduct has evil posthumous titles—generally, hearing the posthumous title one knows the conduct, using it as encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Good conduct earns a laudatory title, evil conduct a pejorative one; the title reveals the life, serving as encouragement and warning.

sentences.zh: 《六典》：太常博士掌王公以下擬諡，皆跡其功德為之褒貶。

translations.literal: Six Codes: the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician oversees drafting posthumous titles for princes and below, all tracing their merit and virtue to praise or censure.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Codes stipulates that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician drafts posthumous titles for princes and below, praising or censuring according to merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 近者臣僚薨卒，雖官該擬諡，其家自知父祖別無善政，慮定諡之際，斥其繆戾，皆不請諡。

translations.literal: Recently when officials and ministers died, although their rank qualified them for posthumous titles, their families, knowing their fathers and grandfathers had no good governance, fearing that when fixing the posthumous title their errors would be exposed, all did not request posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when officials died eligible for posthumous titles, their families—knowing their forebears had no worthy achievements and fearing exposure of their failings—declined to request posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 竊惟 諡法自周公以來，垂為不刊之典，蓋以彰善癉惡，激濁揚清，使其身沒之後，是非較然，用為勸懲。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the posthumous title canon since the Duke of Zhou has been handed down as an immutable institution, generally to display good and hide evil, stir the muddy and raise the clear, so that after the body perishes, right and wrong are clearly compared, used as encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title canon, established since the Duke of Zhou, is an immutable institution for displaying virtue and exposing vice, stirring the muddy and raising the clear, so that after death right and wrong stand clear as encouragement and warning.

sentences.zh: 今若任其遷避，則為惡者肆誌而不悛。

translations.literal: Now if they are allowed to evade and avoid, then those who do evil will indulge their will without repentance.
translations.idiomatic: If evasion is permitted, the wicked will indulge themselves without repentance.

sentences.zh: 乞自今後不必候其請諡， 並令有司舉行，如此，則隱慝無行之人，有所沮勸。

translations.literal: Your servant requests that from now on it is not necessary to wait for them to request posthumous titles; all order relevant offices to carry it out; thus, those who hide shame and lack conduct will have something to deter and encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: I request that henceforth relevant offices proceed without waiting for a family's request, so that those who conceal their shame may be deterred.

sentences.zh: 若須行狀申乞方行擬諡，考諸方冊，別無明證。

translations.literal: If a conduct summary must be submitted and requested before drafting a posthumous title, examining various records, there is no clear evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Requiring a family's petition and conduct summary before drafting a posthumous title finds no clear support in historical records.

sentences.zh: 惟衛公叔文子卒，其子戍請諡。

translations.literal: Only when Duke Wei Gongsun Wenzi died did his son Shu request a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Duke Wei Gongsun Wenzi died did his son Shu request a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 臣謂春秋之時，禮壞樂闕，公叔 之卒，有司不能明舉舊典，故至將葬，始請諡於君。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in Spring and Autumn times, ritual was broken and music lost; when Gongsun died, the relevant offices could not clearly carry out the old canon; therefore only when about to bury did they first request a posthumous title from the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in Spring and Autumn times, when ritual had decayed, the relevant offices failed to carry out the old canon at Gongsun Wenzi's death; only at the point of burial did his son request a posthumous title from the ruler.

sentences.zh: 且周制，太史掌小喪賜諡，小史掌卿大夫之家賜諡請誄。

translations.literal: Moreover, under Zhou institutions, the Grand Scribe oversaw granting posthumous titles for lesser mourning; the Junior Scribe oversaw granting posthumous titles and requesting eulogies for ministers' and grandees' households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou institutions, the Grand Scribe granted posthumous titles for lesser mourning, and the Junior Scribe granted posthumous titles and requested eulogies for ministers and grandees.

sentences.zh: 以此知有司之職，自當舉行，明矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the duty of relevant offices is naturally to carry it out—clear indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that relevant offices were duty-bound to proceed on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 」詔下有司詳定， 如皞請焉。

translations.literal: " An edict sent down to relevant offices for detailed fixing, as Hao requested.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to relevant offices for deliberation, as Wang Hao had requested.

sentences.zh: 禮院更議贈安遠軍節度使馬懷德已葬請諡，乃言：「自古作諡，皆在葬前。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ritual further deliberated on the posthumously granted military commissioner of Anyuan Army Ma Huai'de, already buried, requesting a posthumous title, and said: "From antiquity, making posthumous titles has all been before burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Ritual reconsidered the case of Ma Huai'de, posthumously granted military commissioner of Anyuan, who had already been buried and whose family now requested a posthumous title, it observed: "From antiquity, posthumous titles were conferred before burial.

sentences.zh: 唐《開元》，三品以上將葬，既啟殯，告贈諡於柩前；

translations.literal: Tang Kaiyuan: third rank and above, about to bury, after opening the encoffining, announce the granted posthumous title before the coffin;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Kaiyuan regulations stipulated that for third rank and above, after opening the encoffining and before burial, the granted posthumous title was announced before the coffin;

sentences.zh: 無贈者， 設啟奠即告諡。

translations.literal: For those without grants, upon setting the opening libation, immediately announce the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: where no posthumous grant was involved, the posthumous title was announced at the opening libation.

sentences.zh: 既葬加諡，出於唐時。

translations.literal: Adding posthumous titles after burial originated in Tang times.
translations.idiomatic: Adding posthumous titles after burial originated in Tang times.

sentences.zh: 如顏杲卿、盧弈盡忠王室，當時置而不議。

translations.literal: Such as Yan Gaoqing and Lu Yi, who exhausted loyalty to the royal house—at the time they were set aside without deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing and Lu Yi, who gave their lives for the throne, were at the time passed over without deliberation.

sentences.zh: 至郭知運死五十餘年乃始請諡，右司員外郎崔原以為非旌善之禮，而太常博士獨孤 及謂新製死不必有諡，又謂有故闕禮，追遠請諡，順也。

translations.literal: When Guo Zhiyun died, more than fifty years later they first requested a posthumous title; Right Department Assistant Director Cui Yuan held that this was not the rite of displaying good; but Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Du Gongji said the new regulation that the dead need not have posthumous titles, and also said that when there is cause and ritual is lacking, seeking a posthumous title in reverence for the distant is compliant.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zhiyun's family first requested a posthumous title more than fifty years after his death, Assistant Director Cui Yuan held this violated the rite of honoring virtue; but ritual academician Du Gongji argued that the new Tang regulation did not require posthumous titles, and that when ritual had been omitted for cause, a belated request was proper.

sentences.zh: 及長於開元之世。

translations.literal: Ji grew up in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gongji had grown up in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 親聞啟奠告諡，而謂新製不必有諡，豈非誣哉？

translations.literal: He personally heard the opening libation announce the posthumous title, yet said the new regulation need not have posthumous titles—is this not deception?
translations.idiomatic: He had personally witnessed posthumous titles announced at opening libations, yet claimed the new regulations did not require them—is this not self-contradiction?

sentences.zh: 又有故闕禮，追遠請諡，皆違禮經，何順 之有？

translations.literal: Also, when there is cause and ritual is lacking, seeking a posthumous title in reverence for the distant—all violate the ritual canon; what compliance is there?
translations.idiomatic: As for claiming that omitted ritual justified a belated request—both violate the ritual canon; where is the propriety?

sentences.zh: 國家給諡，一用唐令，然請諡之家，例供尚書省官酒食，撰議官又當有所贈遺，故或闕而不請。

translations.literal: Our state grants posthumous titles, entirely using Tang regulations; yet families requesting posthumous titles customarily supply wine and food to Department of State Affairs officials; drafting officials also should receive gifts; therefore some omit and do not request.
translations.idiomatic: The Song followed Tang regulations for posthumous titles, yet families requesting titles customarily supplied wine and food to Department officials and gave gifts to drafting officials; some therefore declined to request titles at all.

sentences.zh: 景祐四年，宋綬建議，令官給酒食。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyou, Song Shou proposed, ordering the state to supply wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingyou (1037), Song Shou proposed that the state supply wine and food instead.

sentences.zh: 其後，又罷贈遺。

translations.literal: Afterward, gifts were again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts to drafting officials were subsequently abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 自此， 既葬請諡者甚眾。

translations.literal: From this time, those requesting posthumous titles after burial were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, requests for posthumous titles after burial became very common.

sentences.zh: 歲月浸久，官閥行跡，士大夫所不能知，子孫與其門生故吏，志在虛美隱惡，而有司據以加諡，是廢聖人之法，而褟唐庸有司之議也。

translations.literal: As years gradually lengthen, official pedigree and conduct—what scholar-officials cannot know—descendants and their students and former subordinates, intent on empty praise and hiding evil, and relevant offices relying on this to add posthumous titles—this abandons the sages' law and slavishly follows Tang mediocre officials' views.
translations.idiomatic: As years pass, official pedigree and conduct become unknown even to scholar-officials; descendants, students, and former subordinates, intent on empty praise and concealing faults, supply the materials on which officials grant posthumous titles—thus abandoning the sages' method and slavishly following the views of mediocre Tang officials.

sentences.zh: 」詔：「自 今得諡者，令葬前奏請；

translations.literal: " An edict: "From now on, those who receive posthumous titles—order memorial before burial;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Henceforth, those eligible for posthumous titles must petition before burial;

sentences.zh: 或其家不請，則尚書、太常合議定諡，前葬牒史館及付其家。

translations.literal: Or if their family does not request, then the Department of State Affairs and Court of Imperial Sacrifices jointly deliberate and fix the posthumous title, before burial deliver the patent to the Historiography Institute and grant it to their family.
translations.idiomatic: if the family does not petition, the Department of State Affairs and Court of Imperial Sacrifices shall jointly determine the title, record it with the Historiography Institute before burial, and grant it to the family.

sentences.zh: 即褟私諡不以實，論如選舉不以實法。

translations.literal: Private posthumous titles that do not accord with reality shall be prosecuted under the same statute as untruthful recommendations in official selection.
translations.idiomatic: Private posthumous titles that do not reflect the truth shall be prosecuted under the same law that punishes untruthful recommendations in official selection.

sentences.zh: 既葬請諡者，不定諡。」

translations.literal: Those who request posthumous titles after burial shall not be granted posthumous titles."
translations.idiomatic: Those who petition for a posthumous title only after burial shall not be granted one."
